lessons.title: Review Exercise 4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater than the number lying to the left.
  • Every positive integer is greater than every negative integer.
  • The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive. A negative integer is always less than a positive integer.
  • First simplify each side, then compare. A negative integer is always less than a positive integer.
  • The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive.
  • On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater. 0 lies to the right of every negative integer.

Review Exercise 4

  • Fill in the blank: 1(i). −1 is negative integer
  • Fill in the blank: 1(ii). '0' is neither positive nor negative
  • Fill in the blank: 1(iii). −2 is greater than −3
  • Fill in the blank: 1(iv). |−4| = 4
  • True or False: 2(i). −1 < 0 — True
  • True or False: 2(ii). |−2| = −2 — False — |−2| = 2, because the absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive.
  • True or False: 2(iii). (−1) + (−2) = −3 — True
  • True or False: 2(iv). (+2) ÷ (−1) = +2 — False — (+2) ÷ (−1) = −2, because the quotient of two integers with unlike signs is negative.
  • MCQ: 3(i). Choose the correct answer: (+3) × (−2) =
    (a) 6   (b) −6   (c) 1
    Correct answer: −6
  • MCQ: 3(ii). Choose the correct answer: |−4| =
    (a) 4   (b) −4   (c) ±4
    Correct answer: 4
  • MCQ: 3(iii). Choose the correct answer: −1 □ 0
    (a) =   (b) <   (c) >
    Correct answer: <
  • MCQ: 3(iv). Choose the correct answer: (+12) ÷ (−3) =
    (a) +4   (b) −4   (c) 9
    Correct answer: −4
  • Q: 4(i). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: −6 Δ −7
    Ans: Rule: On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater than the number lying to the left.
    Step 1: −6 lies to the right of −7 on the number line.
    Step 2: So −6 is greater than −7.
    Answer: −6 > −7
  • Q: 4(ii). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: 2 Δ −5
    Ans: Rule: Every positive integer is greater than every negative integer.
    Step 1: 2 is a positive integer and −5 is a negative integer.
    Step 2: So 2 is greater than −5.
    Answer: 2 > −5
  • Q: 4(iii). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: −7 Δ |−7|
    Ans: Rule: The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive. A negative integer is always less than a positive integer.
    Step 1: Find the absolute value: |−7| = 7.
    Step 2: Compare −7 with 7. −7 is negative and 7 is positive, so −7 is less than 7.
    Answer: −7 < |−7|
  • Q: 4(iv). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: −|9| Δ −(−9)
    Ans: Rule: First simplify each side, then compare. A negative integer is always less than a positive integer.
    Step 1: −|9| = −9, because |9| = 9.
    Step 2: −(−9) = +9, because the opposite of −9 is +9.
    Step 3: Compare −9 with +9. −9 is less than +9.
    Answer: −|9| < −(−9)
  • Q: 4(v). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: |−3| Δ 3
    Ans: Rule: The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive.
    Step 1: Find the absolute value: |−3| = 3.
    Step 2: Compare 3 with 3. Both are equal.
    Answer: |−3| = 3
  • Q: 4(vi). Use =, > or < sign to indicate the relationship between the pair of numbers: 0 Δ −2
    Ans: Rule: On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater. 0 lies to the right of every negative integer.
    Step 1: −2 lies to the left of 0 on the number line.
    Step 2: So 0 is greater than −2.
    Answer: 0 > −2

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: -1 is a _____ integer.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Integers with a minus sign, lying to the left of 0 on the number line, are negative integers. Step 2: -1 has a minus sign and lies to the left of 0. So -1 is a negative integer.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 0 is neither positive nor _____.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Positive integers lie to the right of 0 and negative integers lie to the left of 0. Step 2: 0 itself is in the middle; it is neither positive nor negative. So the missing word is negative.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: -2 _____ -3.
mcqs.why: Step 1: On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater. Step 2: -2 lies to the right of -3, because -2 is closer to 0. Step 3: So -2 is greater than -3.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true?
mcqs.why: Step 1: On the number line, -1 lies to the left of 0. Step 2: The number lying to the left is smaller than the number lying to the right. Step 3: So -1 is less than 0, written -1 < 0, which is true.

mcqs.q: What is |-2|?
mcqs.why: Rule: The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive (never negative). Step 1: -2 is 2 units away from 0. Step 2: So |-2| = 2. Note: The statement |-2| = -2 is false, because an absolute value cannot be negative.

Rule for like signs: add the absolute values and give the result the common sign. Step 1: |-1| = 1 and |-2| = 2. Step 2: 1 + 2 = 3. Step 3: The common sign is negative, so (-1) + (-2) = -3, so the statement (-1) + (-2) = -3 is true.

Rule: The quotient of two integers with unlike signs is negative. Step 1: The signs are unlike (+ and -), so the quotient will be negative. Step 2: Divide absolute values: 2 / 1 = 2. Step 3: Give the negative sign: (+2) / (-1) = -2. Note: The statement (+2) / (-1) = +2 is false.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct answer: (+3) x (-2) = ?
mcqs.why: Rule: The product of two integers with unlike signs is negative; multiply the absolute values and put a negative sign. Step 1: The signs are unlike (+ and -), so the product will be negative. Step 2: Multiply absolute values: 3 x 2 = 6. Step 3: Give the negative sign: (+3) x (-2) = -6.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct answer: |-4| = ?
mcqs.why: Rule: The absolute value of an integer is its distance from 0 and is always positive. Step 1: -4 is 4 units away from 0 on the number line. Step 2: Distance is always positive, so |-4| = 4.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct answer: -1 ___ 0. Which sign completes this correctly?
mcqs.why: Step 1: On the number line, -1 lies to the left of 0. Step 2: The number lying to the left is smaller than the number lying to the right. Step 3: So -1 is less than 0, and the correct sign is <.

mcqs.q: Choose the correct answer: (+12) / (-3) = ?
mcqs.why: Rule: The quotient of two integers with unlike signs is negative. Step 1: The signs are unlike (+ and -), so the quotient will be negative. Step 2: Divide absolute values: 12 / 3 = 4, because 3 x 4 = 12. Step 3: Give the negative sign: (+12) / (-3) = -4.

mcqs.q: Use =, > or <: -6 ___ -7. Which sign is correct?
mcqs.why: Rule: On the number line, the number lying to the right is greater than the number lying to the left. Step 1: -6 lies to the right of -7 on the number line. Step 2: So -6 is greater than -7, and the correct sign is >.

mcqs.q: Use =, > or <: -7 ___ |-7|. Which sign is correct?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the absolute value: |-7| = 7, because the absolute value is the distance from 0 and is always positive. Step 2: Compare -7 with 7. Step 3: A negative integer is always less than a positive integer, so -7 < |-7| and the correct sign is <.

mcqs.q: Use =, > or <: -|9| ___ -(-9). Which sign is correct?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Simplify the left side: |9| = 9, so -|9| = -9. Step 2: Simplify the right side: -(-9) = +9, because the opposite of -9 is +9. Step 3: Compare -9 with +9: a negative integer is less than a positive integer, so -|9| < -(-9) and the correct sign is <.

mcqs.q: Use =, > or <: |-3| ___ 3. Which sign is correct?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the absolute value: |-3| = 3, because -3 is 3 units away from 0 and absolute value is always positive. Step 2: Compare 3 with 3. Step 3: Both sides are the same number, so |-3| = 3 and the correct sign is =.

lessons.title: Exercises 5.1 and 5.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • BODMAS bracket order: vinculum (bar) first, then ( ), then { }, then [ ].
  • Inside brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction, working left to right.
  • Subtracting a negative integer means adding its opposite, e.g. 8 - (-4) = 8 + 4 = 12.
  • For fractions, make denominators equal using the LCM before adding or subtracting; change mixed fractions to improper fractions first.

Exercise 5.1

  • Q: Simplify the following: 1. 8 − (3 − 5+2), where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 5+2
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 5 + 2 = 7.
    The expression becomes: 8 − (3 − 7)
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 3 − 7 = −4.
    The expression becomes: 8 − (−4)
    Step 3: Subtracting a negative integer means adding its opposite: 8 − (−4) = 8 + 4.
    Step 4: Add: 8 + 4 = 12.
    Answer: 12
  • Q: Simplify the following: 2. 10 − [8 − {5 − (2 − 3+6)}], where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 3+6
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 3 + 6 = 9.
    The expression becomes: 10 − [8 − {5 − (2 − 9)}]
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 2 − 9 = −7.
    The expression becomes: 10 − [8 − {5 − (−7)}]
    Step 3: Remove the braces { }: 5 − (−7) = 5 + 7 = 12.
    The expression becomes: 10 − [8 − 12]
    Step 4: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 8 − 12 = −4.
    The expression becomes: 10 − (−4)
    Step 5: Subtract: 10 − (−4) = 10 + 4 = 14.
    Answer: 14
  • Q: Simplify the following: 3. 30 − 2[5 − {15 ÷ 3×4 − (3 − 5−3)}], where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 5−3
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 5 − 3 = 2.
    The expression becomes: 30 − 2[5 − {15 ÷ 3×4 − (3 − 2)}]
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 3 − 2 = 1.
    The expression becomes: 30 − 2[5 − {15 ÷ 3×4 − 1}]
    Step 3: Inside the braces { }, do division and multiplication from left to right first: 15 ÷ 3 = 5, then 5 × 4 = 20.
    The expression becomes: 30 − 2[5 − {20 − 1}]
    Step 4: Remove the braces { }: 20 − 1 = 19.
    The expression becomes: 30 − 2[5 − 19]
    Step 5: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 5 − 19 = −14.
    The expression becomes: 30 − 2 × (−14)
    Step 6: Multiply before subtracting: 2 × (−14) = −28.
    The expression becomes: 30 − (−28)
    Step 7: Subtract: 30 − (−28) = 30 + 28 = 58.
    Answer: 58
  • Q: Simplify the following: 4. 5/2 + (2/3 − 5/6)
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first. Inside, make the denominators equal. The LCM of 3 and 6 is 6.
    2/3 = 4/6, so 2/3 − 5/6 = 4/6 − 5/6 = −1/6.
    The expression becomes: 5/2 + (−1/6)
    Step 2: Add the fractions. The LCM of 2 and 6 is 6.
    5/2 = 15/6, so 15/6 + (−1/6) = 15/6 − 1/6 = 14/6.
    Step 3: Reduce to lowest terms: 14/6 = 7/3 = 2 1/3.
    Answer: 7/3 or 2 1/3
  • Q: Simplify the following: 5. 3 5/8 − {3/8 − (3/4 + 5/8)}
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first. The LCM of 4 and 8 is 8.
    3/4 = 6/8, so 3/4 + 5/8 = 6/8 + 5/8 = 11/8.
    The expression becomes: 3 5/8 − {3/8 − 11/8}
    Step 2: Remove the braces { }: 3/8 − 11/8 = −8/8 = −1.
    The expression becomes: 3 5/8 − (−1)
    Step 3: Change the mixed fraction into an improper fraction: 3 5/8 = 29/8.
    Step 4: Subtract: 29/8 − (−1) = 29/8 + 8/8 = 37/8.
    Step 5: Change back into a mixed fraction: 37/8 = 4 5/8.
    Answer: 4 5/8
  • Q: Simplify the following: 6. 3/2 + {1/2 + (3/4 ÷ 2 1/4)}
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first. Change the mixed fraction into an improper fraction: 2 1/4 = 9/4.
    Step 2: Divide: 3/4 ÷ 9/4 = 3/4 × 4/9 = 12/36 = 1/3.
    The expression becomes: 3/2 + {1/2 + 1/3}
    Step 3: Remove the braces { }. The LCM of 2 and 3 is 6.
    1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.
    The expression becomes: 3/2 + 5/6
    Step 4: Add. The LCM of 2 and 6 is 6.
    3/2 = 9/6, so 9/6 + 5/6 = 14/6 = 7/3 = 2 1/3.
    Answer: 7/3 or 2 1/3
  • Q: Simplify the following: 7. 2 1/4 − [3/2 ÷ {(5/2 − 1/4) × 4/3}]
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first. The LCM of 2 and 4 is 4.
    5/2 = 10/4, so 5/2 − 1/4 = 10/4 − 1/4 = 9/4.
    The expression becomes: 2 1/4 − [3/2 ÷ {9/4 × 4/3}]
    Step 2: Remove the braces { }: 9/4 × 4/3 = 36/12 = 3.
    The expression becomes: 2 1/4 − [3/2 ÷ 3]
    Step 3: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 3/2 ÷ 3 = 3/2 × 1/3 = 3/6 = 1/2.
    The expression becomes: 2 1/4 − 1/2
    Step 4: Change the mixed fraction into an improper fraction: 2 1/4 = 9/4.
    Step 5: Subtract: 9/4 − 1/2 = 9/4 − 2/4 = 7/4 = 1 3/4.
    Answer: 7/4 or 1 3/4
  • Q: Simplify the following: 8. 2 1/3 ÷ [2 5/6 ÷ {1 1/2 + (3 1/2 × 2 2/3 − 1 1/6)}], where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 2 2/3 − 1 1/6
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Change all mixed fractions into improper fractions: 2 1/3 = 7/3, 2 5/6 = 17/6, 1 1/2 = 3/2, 3 1/2 = 7/2, 2 2/3 = 8/3, 1 1/6 = 7/6.
    The expression becomes: 7/3 ÷ [17/6 ÷ {3/2 + (7/2 × (8/3 − 7/6))}], where the bar group is (8/3 − 7/6).
    Step 2: Remove the vinculum first. The LCM of 3 and 6 is 6.
    8/3 = 16/6, so 8/3 − 7/6 = 16/6 − 7/6 = 9/6 = 3/2.
    Step 3: Remove the parentheses ( ): multiply first, 7/2 × 3/2 = 21/4.
    The expression becomes: 7/3 ÷ [17/6 ÷ {3/2 + 21/4}]
    Step 4: Remove the braces { }. The LCM of 2 and 4 is 4.
    3/2 = 6/4, so 6/4 + 21/4 = 27/4.
    The expression becomes: 7/3 ÷ [17/6 ÷ 27/4]
    Step 5: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 17/6 ÷ 27/4 = 17/6 × 4/27 = 68/162 = 34/81.
    The expression becomes: 7/3 ÷ 34/81
    Step 6: Divide: 7/3 × 81/34 = 567/102 = 189/34.
    Step 7: Change into a mixed fraction: 189/34 = 5 19/34.
    Answer: 189/34 or 5 19/34

Exercise 5.2

  • Q: Simplify the following: 1. 1.4 + (1.6 − 0.3)
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first: 1.6 − 0.3 = 1.3.
    The expression becomes: 1.4 + 1.3
    Step 2: Add: 1.4 + 1.3 = 2.7.
    Answer: 2.7
  • Q: Simplify the following: 2. 4.26 + [1.35 ÷ {(0.5 − 0.3) × 1.5}]
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first: 0.5 − 0.3 = 0.2.
    The expression becomes: 4.26 + [1.35 ÷ {0.2 × 1.5}]
    Step 2: Remove the braces { }: 0.2 × 1.5 = 0.30.
    The expression becomes: 4.26 + [1.35 ÷ 0.30]
    Step 3: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 1.35 ÷ 0.30 = 4.5.
    The expression becomes: 4.26 + 4.5
    Step 4: Add: 4.26 + 4.5 = 8.76.
    Answer: 8.76
  • Q: Simplify the following: 3. 1.9 × [2.3 × {3.6 − (1.2 + 1.4)}]
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first: 1.2 + 1.4 = 2.6.
    The expression becomes: 1.9 × [2.3 × {3.6 − 2.6}]
    Step 2: Remove the braces { }: 3.6 − 2.6 = 1.0.
    The expression becomes: 1.9 × [2.3 × 1.0]
    Step 3: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 2.3 × 1.0 = 2.3.
    The expression becomes: 1.9 × 2.3
    Step 4: Multiply: 1.9 × 2.3 = 4.37.
    Answer: 4.37
  • Q: Simplify the following: 4. 9.25 ÷ [1.75 + {2.05 − (1.5 + 2.5−2)}], where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 2.5−2
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 2.5 − 2 = 0.5.
    The expression becomes: 9.25 ÷ [1.75 + {2.05 − (1.5 + 0.5)}]
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 1.5 + 0.5 = 2.0.
    The expression becomes: 9.25 ÷ [1.75 + {2.05 − 2.0}]
    Step 3: Remove the braces { }: 2.05 − 2.0 = 0.05.
    The expression becomes: 9.25 ÷ [1.75 + 0.05]
    Step 4: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 1.75 + 0.05 = 1.80.
    The expression becomes: 9.25 ÷ 1.8
    Step 5: Divide: 9.25 ÷ 1.8 = 925/180 = 185/36 = 5 5/36, which is approximately 5.14.
    Answer: 185/36 or 5 5/36 (approximately 5.14)
    Note: As printed in the book, the last division 9.25 ÷ 1.8 does not give a whole number, so the exact answer is the fraction 185/36.
  • Q: Simplify the following: 5. 2.9 − [1.05 × {1.17 + (2.5 + 1.9−0.4)}], where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 1.9−0.4
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 1.9 − 0.4 = 1.5.
    The expression becomes: 2.9 − [1.05 × {1.17 + (2.5 + 1.5)}]
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 2.5 + 1.5 = 4.0.
    The expression becomes: 2.9 − [1.05 × {1.17 + 4.0}]
    Step 3: Remove the braces { }: 1.17 + 4.0 = 5.17.
    The expression becomes: 2.9 − [1.05 × 5.17]
    Step 4: Remove the square brackets [ ]: 1.05 × 5.17 = 5.4285.
    The expression becomes: 2.9 − 5.4285
    Step 5: Subtract: 2.9 − 5.4285 = −2.5285.
    Answer: −2.5285
    Note: As printed in the book, the value inside the square brackets (5.4285) is greater than 2.9, so the final answer is a negative number.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 8 - (3 - [bar over 5+2])
mcqs.why: BODMAS: remove brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 5 + 2 = 7, giving 8 - (3 - 7). Step 2: Remove the parentheses: 3 - 7 = -4, giving 8 - (-4). Step 3: Subtracting a negative means adding its opposite: 8 - (-4) = 8 + 4. Step 4: 8 + 4 = 12.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 10 - [8 - {5 - (2 - [bar over 3+6])}]
mcqs.why: BODMAS order: vinculum, ( ), { }, [ ]. Step 1: Vinculum: 3 + 6 = 9, giving 10 - [8 - {5 - (2 - 9)}]. Step 2: Parentheses: 2 - 9 = -7, giving 10 - [8 - {5 - (-7)}]. Step 3: Braces: 5 - (-7) = 5 + 7 = 12, giving 10 - [8 - 12]. Step 4: Square brackets: 8 - 12 = -4, giving 10 - (-4). Step 5: 10 - (-4) = 10 + 4 = 14.

BODMAS: remove parentheses first. Step 1: Inside the brackets use LCM 6: 2/3 = 4/6, so 2/3 - 5/6 = 4/6 - 5/6 = -1/6, giving 5/2 + (-1/6). Step 2: Add with LCM 6: 5/2 = 15/6, so 15/6 - 1/6 = 14/6. Step 3: Reduce: 14/6 = 7/3 = 2 1/3.

BODMAS: parentheses, then braces. Step 1: Parentheses with LCM 8: 3/4 = 6/8, so 3/4 + 5/8 = 11/8, giving 3 5/8 - {3/8 - 11/8}. Step 2: Braces: 3/8 - 11/8 = -8/8 = -1, giving 3 5/8 - (-1). Step 3: 3 5/8 = 29/8, and 29/8 + 8/8 = 37/8. Step 4: 37/8 = 4 5/8.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 3/2 + {1/2 + (3/4 divided by 2 1/4)}
mcqs.why: BODMAS: parentheses first. Step 1: 2 1/4 = 9/4. Step 2: Divide: 3/4 divided by 9/4 = 3/4 x 4/9 = 12/36 = 1/3, giving 3/2 + {1/2 + 1/3}. Step 3: Braces with LCM 6: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6, giving 3/2 + 5/6. Step 4: Add with LCM 6: 3/2 = 9/6, so 9/6 + 5/6 = 14/6 = 7/3 = 2 1/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2 1/4 - [3/2 divided by {(5/2 - 1/4) x 4/3}]
mcqs.why: BODMAS: parentheses, braces, then square brackets. Step 1: Parentheses with LCM 4: 5/2 = 10/4, so 5/2 - 1/4 = 9/4. Step 2: Braces: 9/4 x 4/3 = 36/12 = 3, giving 2 1/4 - [3/2 divided by 3]. Step 3: Brackets: 3/2 divided by 3 = 3/2 x 1/3 = 1/2. Step 4: 2 1/4 = 9/4, and 9/4 - 1/2 = 9/4 - 2/4 = 7/4 = 1 3/4.
BODMAS: remove the parentheses first. Step 1: 1.6 - 0.3 = 1.3, giving 1.4 + 1.3. Step 2: Add: 1.4 + 1.3 = 2.7.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 4.26 + [1.35 divided by {(0.5 - 0.3) x 1.5}]
mcqs.why: BODMAS: parentheses, braces, then square brackets. Step 1: Parentheses: 0.5 - 0.3 = 0.2, giving 4.26 + [1.35 divided by {0.2 x 1.5}]. Step 2: Braces: 0.2 x 1.5 = 0.30, giving 4.26 + [1.35 divided by 0.30]. Step 3: Brackets: 1.35 divided by 0.30 = 4.5, giving 4.26 + 4.5. Step 4: Add: 4.26 + 4.5 = 8.76.

BODMAS: parentheses, braces, then square brackets. Step 1: Parentheses: 1.2 + 1.4 = 2.6, giving 1.9 x [2.3 x {3.6 - 2.6}]. Step 2: Braces: 3.6 - 2.6 = 1.0, giving 1.9 x [2.3 x 1.0]. Step 3: Brackets: 2.3 x 1.0 = 2.3, giving 1.9 x 2.3. Step 4: Multiply: 1.9 x 2.3 = 4.37.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 30 - 2[5 - {15 divided by 3 x 4 - (3 - [bar over 5-3])}]
mcqs.why: BODMAS: vinculum, parentheses, braces (division and multiplication before subtraction), then brackets. Step 1: Vinculum: 5 - 3 = 2. Step 2: Parentheses: 3 - 2 = 1. Step 3: Inside braces, 15 divided by 3 = 5, then 5 x 4 = 20, then 20 - 1 = 19. Step 4: Brackets: 5 - 19 = -14, giving 30 - 2 x (-14). Step 5: Multiply: 2 x (-14) = -28, giving 30 - (-28). Step 6: 30 + 28 = 58.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To find the total quantity sold, add all the three quantities.
  • The carpet needed for a floor is equal to the area of the floor. Area of a rectangle = length × width.
  • First find the rent from the total income, subtract it, and then find the amount spent on necessities from the remaining amount.
  • First find Ghazala's share of the 40 toffees, and then find 1/6 of that share.
  • Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
  • The total distance is found by adding the two distances. How much more one distance is than the other is found by subtracting the smaller from the larger.

Exercise 5.3

  • Q: 1. A shopkeeper sold 5 1/2 kg sugar, 4 1/4 kg maize and 10 3/4 kg flour to three customers. How much did he sell in all?
    Ans: Rule: To find the total quantity sold, add all the three quantities.
    Step 1: Write the quantities: sugar = 5 1/2 kg, maize = 4 1/4 kg, flour = 10 3/4 kg.
    Step 2: Change the mixed fractions into improper fractions: 5 1/2 = 11/2, 4 1/4 = 17/4, 10 3/4 = 43/4.
    Step 3: Make the denominators equal. The LCM of 2 and 4 is 4, and 11/2 = 22/4.
    Step 4: Add: 22/4 + 17/4 + 43/4 = 82/4.
    Step 5: Simplify: 82/4 = 41/2 = 20 1/2.
    Answer: The shopkeeper sold 20 1/2 kg in all.
  • Q: 2. A room is 5 1/2 metre long and 3 1/4 metre wide. How much square metre carpet is required for its floor?
    Ans: Rule: The carpet needed for a floor is equal to the area of the floor. Area of a rectangle = length × width.
    Step 1: Length = 5 1/2 metre and width = 3 1/4 metre.
    Step 2: Change the mixed fractions into improper fractions: 5 1/2 = 11/2 and 3 1/4 = 13/4.
    Step 3: Multiply: 11/2 × 13/4 = 143/8.
    Step 4: Change into a mixed fraction: 143/8 = 17 7/8.
    Answer: 17 7/8 square metres of carpet is required.
  • Q: 3. Nasir's total income is Rs. 10,000. He paid 1/10 of his income as house rent and 1/4 of the remaining on other necessities. What amount has been left with him?
    Ans: Rule: First find the rent from the total income, subtract it, and then find the amount spent on necessities from the remaining amount.
    Step 1: Total income = Rs.10,000.
    Step 2: House rent = 1/10 of 10,000 = 1/10 × 10,000 = Rs.1,000.
    Step 3: Remaining amount = 10,000 − 1,000 = Rs.9,000.
    Step 4: Amount spent on other necessities = 1/4 of 9,000 = 1/4 × 9,000 = Rs.2,250.
    Step 5: Amount left = 9,000 − 2,250 = Rs.6,750.
    Answer: Rs.6,750 has been left with him.
  • Q: 4. Tasneem has 40 toffees. She gave 3/5 of it to Ghazala. Ghazala gave 1/6 of her own share to her younger brother. How much toffees Ghazala's brother got?
    Ans: Rule: First find Ghazala's share of the 40 toffees, and then find 1/6 of that share.
    Step 1: Total toffees = 40.
    Step 2: Ghazala's share = 3/5 of 40 = 3/5 × 40 = 24 toffees.
    Step 3: The brother's share = 1/6 of Ghazala's share = 1/6 × 24 = 4 toffees.
    Answer: Ghazala's brother got 4 toffees.
  • Q: 5. How much time Waseem will take to cover 50.5 kilometres distance with a speed of 12.25 kilometers per hour?
    Ans: Rule: Time = Distance ÷ Speed.
    Step 1: Distance = 50.5 kilometres and speed = 12.25 kilometres per hour.
    Step 2: Time = 50.5 ÷ 12.25.
    Step 3: Remove the decimals by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 100: 50.5/12.25 = 5050/1225.
    Step 4: Reduce the fraction: 5050/1225 = 202/49.
    Step 5: Divide: 202 ÷ 49 = 4.1224..., which is approximately 4.12.
    Answer: Waseem will take approximately 4.12 hours.
    Note: As printed in the book, 50.5 ÷ 12.25 is not exact; the exact time is 202/49 hours, about 4.12 hours.
  • Q: 6. Shahab travelled 4.7 km distance on foot, 15.5 km distance by bicycle. How much distance traveled altogether? Also tell how much more distance he traveled by bicycle than on foot?
    Ans: Rule: The total distance is found by adding the two distances. How much more one distance is than the other is found by subtracting the smaller from the larger.
    Step 1: Distance on foot = 4.7 km and distance by bicycle = 15.5 km.
    Step 2: Total distance = 4.7 + 15.5 = 20.2 km.
    Step 3: More distance by bicycle = 15.5 − 4.7 = 10.8 km.
    Answer: He travelled 20.2 km altogether, and he travelled 10.8 km more by bicycle than on foot.
  • Q: 7. The price of one dozen eggs is Rs.60.50. Find the price of one egg?
    Ans: Rule: One dozen = 12. The price of one egg = price of one dozen ÷ 12.
    Step 1: Price of 12 eggs = Rs.60.50.
    Step 2: Price of one egg = 60.50 ÷ 12.
    Step 3: Divide: 60.50 ÷ 12 = 5.0416..., which is approximately 5.04.
    Answer: The price of one egg is approximately Rs.5.04.
    Note: As printed in the book, Rs.60.50 ÷ 12 is not exact; the exact value is about Rs.5.04.
  • Q: 8. A bamboo is 24 metres long, its 0.75 part is above the ground and remaining part is inside the ground. How many metres bamboo inside the ground?
    Ans: Rule: First find the part above the ground, and then subtract it from the total length to get the part inside the ground.
    Step 1: Total length of the bamboo = 24 metres.
    Step 2: Part above the ground = 0.75 of 24 = 0.75 × 24 = 18 metres.
    Step 3: Part inside the ground = 24 − 18 = 6 metres.
    Answer: 6 metres of the bamboo is inside the ground.
  • Q: 9. The total population of a village is 6000. Out of this 0.05 of the population is in service, 0.4 of it is in trade and 0.06 of it are labourers. The rest of population is jobless. Tell how many are jobless?
    Ans: Rule: Find the number of people in service, in trade and working as labourers, add them, and subtract the sum from the total population.
    Step 1: Total population = 6000.
    Step 2: People in service = 0.05 × 6000 = 300.
    Step 3: People in trade = 0.4 × 6000 = 2400.
    Step 4: Labourers = 0.06 × 6000 = 360.
    Step 5: Total people with work = 300 + 2400 + 360 = 3060.
    Step 6: Jobless people = 6000 − 3060 = 2940.
    Answer: 2940 people are jobless.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper sold 5 1/2 kg sugar, 4 1/4 kg maize and 10 3/4 kg flour. How much did he sell in all?
mcqs.why: To find the total, add all three quantities. Step 1: Change to improper fractions: 5 1/2 = 11/2, 4 1/4 = 17/4, 10 3/4 = 43/4. Step 2: Use LCM 4: 11/2 = 22/4. Step 3: Add: 22/4 + 17/4 + 43/4 = 82/4. Step 4: Simplify: 82/4 = 41/2 = 20 1/2. Hence he sold 20 1/2 kg in all.

mcqs.q: A room is 5 1/2 metre long and 3 1/4 metre wide. How much carpet is required for its floor?
mcqs.why: Formula: Area of a rectangle = length x width, and the carpet needed equals the floor area. Step 1: Length = 5 1/2 = 11/2 and width = 3 1/4 = 13/4. Step 2: Multiply: 11/2 x 13/4 = 143/8. Step 3: Change to a mixed fraction: 143/8 = 17 7/8. Hence 17 7/8 square metres of carpet is required.

mcqs.q: Nasir's income is Rs. 10,000. He paid 1/10 as house rent and 1/4 of the remaining on other necessities. How much is left with him?
Tasneem has 40 toffees. She gave 3/5 of them to Ghazala, and Ghazala gave 1/6 of her share to her brother. How many toffees did Ghazala's brother get?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Ghazala's share = 3/5 of 40 = 3/5 x 40 = 24 toffees. Step 2: Brother's share = 1/6 of Ghazala's share = 1/6 x 24 = 4 toffees. Hence Ghazala's brother got 4 toffees.

mcqs.q: How much time will Waseem take to cover 50.5 km at a speed of 12.25 km per hour?
mcqs.why: Formula: Time = Distance divided by Speed. Step 1: Time = 50.5 divided by 12.25. Step 2: Multiply numerator and denominator by 100: 5050/1225. Step 3: Reduce: 5050/1225 = 202/49. Step 4: 202 divided by 49 = 4.1224..., about 4.12. Note: as printed, the division is not exact; the exact time is 202/49 hours, about 4.12 hours.

mcqs.q: Shahab travelled 4.7 km on foot and 15.5 km by bicycle. How much distance did he travel altogether?
mcqs.why: Total distance is found by adding the two distances. Step 1: Distance on foot = 4.7 km. Step 2: Distance by bicycle = 15.5 km. Step 3: Add: 4.7 + 15.5 = 20.2 km. Hence he travelled 20.2 km altogether.

mcqs.q: Shahab travelled 4.7 km on foot and 15.5 km by bicycle. How much more distance did he travel by bicycle than on foot?
mcqs.why: How much more is found by subtracting the smaller distance from the larger. Step 1: Distance by bicycle = 15.5 km. Step 2: Distance on foot = 4.7 km. Step 3: Subtract: 15.5 - 4.7 = 10.8 km. Hence he travelled 10.8 km more by bicycle than on foot.

mcqs.q: The price of one dozen eggs is Rs. 60.50. What is the price of one egg?
mcqs.why: One dozen = 12, so price of one egg = price of one dozen divided by 12. Step 1: Price of 12 eggs = Rs. 60.50. Step 2: Price of one egg = 60.50 divided by 12. Step 3: 60.50 divided by 12 = 5.0416..., about 5.04. Note: as printed, the division is not exact; the price is about Rs. 5.04.

mcqs.q: A bamboo is 24 metres long. Its 0.75 part is above the ground and the rest is inside the ground. How many metres are inside the ground?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Total length = 24 metres. Step 2: Part above the ground = 0.75 of 24 = 0.75 x 24 = 18 metres. Step 3: Part inside the ground = 24 - 18 = 6 metres. Hence 6 metres of the bamboo is inside the ground.

mcqs.q: The population of a village is 6000. 0.05 are in service, 0.4 in trade and 0.06 are labourers. The rest are jobless. How many are jobless?
mcqs.why: Step 1: In service = 0.05 x 6000 = 300. Step 2: In trade = 0.4 x 6000 = 2400. Step 3: Labourers = 0.06 x 6000 = 360. Step 4: Total with work = 300 + 2400 + 360 = 3060. Step 5: Jobless = 6000 - 3060 = 2940. Hence 2940 people are jobless.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The other fraction = sum of the two fractions − the given fraction.
  • To find the total temperature, add the temperatures of all the four days.
  • BODMAS: Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction; S stands for Subtraction.
  • Bracket order: vinculum (bar), parentheses ( ), braces { }, square brackets [ ] - four types in all.
  • Other fraction = sum of two fractions minus the given fraction.
  • Fare = distance x rate per kilometre.
  • Total of given quantities is found by adding them one by one.

Review Exercise 5

  • MCQ: 1(i). Choose the correct answer: ( ) is
    (a) Vinculum   (b) Parentheses   (c) Braces   (d) Square brackets.
    Correct answer: Parentheses
  • MCQ: 1(ii). Choose the correct answer: Word 'S' used in BODMAS is abbreviation of
    (a) Solution   (b) Subtraction   (c) Square   (d) None
    Correct answer: Subtraction
  • MCQ: 1(iii). Choose the correct answer: Order of brackets is
    (a) Braces, square bracket, vinculum and parenthesis   (b) Vinculum, braces, parenthesis and square bracket.   (c) Vinculum, parenthesis, braces and square brackets.   (d) Parenthesis, vinculum, braces and square brackets.
    Correct answer: Vinculum, parenthesis, braces and square brackets.
  • MCQ: 1(iv). Choose the correct answer: 5.12 − 5.02 is equal to
    (a) 10.14   (b) 0.14   (c) 0.1   (d) 0.01
    Correct answer: 0.1
  • MCQ: 1(v). Choose the correct answer: Brackets are of
    (a) 2 types   (b) 3 types   (c) 4 types   (d) 5 types
    Correct answer: 4 types
  • Q: 2(i). Simplify the following: 1/2 + {5/14 × (25/15 − 21/25)}
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the parentheses ( ) first. The LCM of 15 and 25 is 75.
    25/15 = 125/75 and 21/25 = 63/75, so 25/15 − 21/25 = 125/75 − 63/75 = 62/75.
    The expression becomes: 1/2 + {5/14 × 62/75}
    Step 2: Remove the braces { }: 5/14 × 62/75 = 310/1050 = 31/105.
    The expression becomes: 1/2 + 31/105
    Step 3: Add the fractions. The LCM of 2 and 105 is 210.
    1/2 = 105/210 and 31/105 = 62/210, so 105/210 + 62/210 = 167/210.
    Answer: 167/210
  • Q: 2(ii). Simplify the following: 1.02 + {3.9 × (4.05 − 2.02−0.98)}, where a vinculum (bar) is printed over 2.02−0.98
    Ans: Rule (BODMAS): First remove the brackets in the order vinculum (bar), ( ), { }, [ ]. Inside the brackets, do Division and Multiplication before Addition and Subtraction.
    Step 1: Remove the vinculum first: 2.02 − 0.98 = 1.04.
    The expression becomes: 1.02 + {3.9 × (4.05 − 1.04)}
    Step 2: Remove the parentheses ( ): 4.05 − 1.04 = 3.01.
    The expression becomes: 1.02 + {3.9 × 3.01}
    Step 3: Remove the braces { }: 3.9 × 3.01 = 11.739.
    The expression becomes: 1.02 + 11.739
    Step 4: Add: 1.02 + 11.739 = 12.759.
    Answer: 12.759
  • Q: 2(iii). Sum of two fractions is 10 1/2. If one fraction is 3 6/8, find the other.
    Ans: Rule: The other fraction = sum of the two fractions − the given fraction.
    Step 1: Sum = 10 1/2 and one fraction = 3 6/8.
    Step 2: Change into improper fractions with denominator 8: 10 1/2 = 21/2 = 84/8, and 3 6/8 = 30/8.
    Step 3: Subtract: 84/8 − 30/8 = 54/8.
    Step 4: Simplify: 54/8 = 27/4 = 6 3/4.
    Answer: The other fraction is 6 3/4.
  • Q: 2(iv). What will be the fare for 30075 kilometre at the rate of Rs.2.25 per kilometre?
    Ans: Formula: Fare = distance × rate per kilometre.
    The book prints the distance as '30075 kilometre', which is a misprint for 300.75 kilometre (the decimal point is missing in print; the book's own answer key gives Rs.676.6875, which is 300.75 × 2.25).
    Fare = 300.75 × 2.25
    300.75 × 2 = 601.50
    300.75 × 0.25 = 75.1875
    Fare = 601.50 + 75.1875 = 676.6875
    Answer: The fare will be Rs.676.6875, i.e. about Rs.676.69.
    Note: Taken exactly as printed (30075 km), the fare would be 30075 × 2.25 = Rs.67,668.75.
  • Q: 2(v). In Peshawar the temperature on one day of June was 45.6°, on second day 43.3°, on the third day 40.5° and the fourth day it was 44.7°. Find the total temperature of four days.
    Ans: Rule: To find the total temperature, add the temperatures of all the four days.
    Step 1: Temperatures are 45.6°, 43.3°, 40.5° and 44.7°.
    Step 2: Add the first two: 45.6 + 43.3 = 88.9.
    Step 3: Add the third: 88.9 + 40.5 = 129.4.
    Step 4: Add the fourth: 129.4 + 44.7 = 174.1.
    Answer: The total temperature of four days is 174.1°.

mcqs.q: ( ) is called:
mcqs.why: The round brackets ( ) are called Parentheses. The bar is the vinculum, { } are braces and [ ] are square brackets. In BODMAS the bracket-removal order is vinculum, parentheses, braces and square brackets.

mcqs.q: The word 'S' used in BODMAS is the abbreviation of:
mcqs.why: In BODMAS, B = Brackets, O = Of, D = Division, M = Multiplication, A = Addition and S = Subtraction. Hence the letter S stands for Subtraction, which is done last in the order of operations.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order of brackets?
options: Braces, square bracket, vinculum and parenthesis
Vinculum, braces, parenthesis and square bracket
Vinculum, parenthesis, braces and square brackets
Parenthesis, vinculum, braces and square brackets
mcqs.why: Brackets are removed in a fixed order: first the vinculum (bar), then the parentheses ( ), then the braces { }, and last the square brackets [ ]. Hence the order is vinculum, parenthesis, braces and square brackets.

mcqs.q: 5.12 - 5.02 is equal to:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Subtract the whole parts and decimal parts: 5.12 - 5.02. Step 2: 5 - 5 = 0 and 0.12 - 0.02 = 0.10. Step 3: So 5.12 - 5.02 = 0.10 = 0.1. Hence the value is 0.1.

mcqs.q: Brackets are of how many types?
mcqs.why: There are four types of brackets: the vinculum (bar), the parentheses ( ), the braces { } and the square brackets [ ]. They are removed in that order when simplifying an expression.

BODMAS: vinculum, parentheses, then braces. Step 1: Vinculum: 2.02 - 0.98 = 1.04, giving 1.02 + {3.9 x (4.05 - 1.04)}. Step 2: Parentheses: 4.05 - 1.04 = 3.01, giving 1.02 + {3.9 x 3.01}. Step 3: Braces: 3.9 x 3.01 = 11.739, giving 1.02 + 11.739. Step 4: Add: 1.02 + 11.739 = 12.759.

mcqs.q: The sum of two fractions is 10 1/2. If one fraction is 3 6/8, what is the other fraction?
mcqs.why: The other fraction = sum - given fraction. Step 1: Sum = 10 1/2 and one fraction = 3 6/8. Step 2: With denominator 8: 10 1/2 = 21/2 = 84/8 and 3 6/8 = 30/8. Step 3: Subtract: 84/8 - 30/8 = 54/8. Step 4: Simplify: 54/8 = 27/4 = 6 3/4. Hence the other fraction is 6 3/4.

mcqs.q: What will be the fare for 300.75 kilometre at the rate of Rs. 2.25 per kilometre?
mcqs.why: Formula: Fare = distance x rate per kilometre. The book prints the distance as 30075 kilometre, which is a misprint: the decimal point is missing and the book answer key Rs. 676.6875 equals 300.75 x 2.25, so the true distance is 300.75 km. Step 1: 300.75 x 2 = 601.50. Step 2: 300.75 x 0.25 = 75.1875. Step 3: Fare = 601.50 + 75.1875 = Rs. 676.6875, about Rs. 676.69. Taken literally as 30075 km the fare would be Rs. 67,668.75, which is not the intended question.

mcqs.q: In Peshawar the temperatures on four days were 45.6, 43.3, 40.5 and 44.7 degrees. What is the total temperature of the four days?
mcqs.why: To find the total, add all four temperatures. Step 1: 45.6 + 43.3 = 88.9. Step 2: 88.9 + 40.5 = 129.4. Step 3: 129.4 + 44.7 = 174.1. Hence the total temperature of the four days is 174.1 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A ratio is reduced to its lowest form by dividing both terms by their HCF.
  • Before writing a ratio, change both quantities to the same unit (kilometers to meters, hours to minutes, years to months).
  • For a ratio with decimals, multiply both terms by 10 or 100 to remove the decimals, then divide by the HCF.
  • When a part of a total is needed first (for example passed = total − failed), find that part before writing the ratio.

Exercise 6.1

  • Q: Q1(i). Find the ratio between the following quantities and reduce them to the lowest form: Rs.450 and Rs.525
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio and divide both terms by their HCF to get the lowest form.
    Ratio = 450 : 525
    Divide both terms by 75.
    450 ÷ 75 = 6
    525 ÷ 75 = 7
    Answer: 6 : 7
  • Q: Q1(ii). Find the ratio between the following quantities and reduce them to the lowest form: 364 cows and 455 cows
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio and divide both terms by their HCF to get the lowest form.
    Ratio = 364 : 455
    Divide both terms by 91.
    364 ÷ 91 = 4
    455 ÷ 91 = 5
    Answer: 4 : 5
  • Q: Q1(iii). Find the ratio between the following quantities and reduce them to the lowest form: 594kg and 990kg.
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio and divide both terms by their HCF to get the lowest form.
    Ratio = 594 : 990
    Divide both terms by 198.
    594 ÷ 198 = 3
    990 ÷ 198 = 5
    Answer: 3 : 5
  • Q: Q1(iv). Find the ratio between the following quantities and reduce them to the lowest form: 1 kilometer, 8 meters and 672 meters.
    Ans: Method: First change both quantities to the same unit, then reduce the ratio by the HCF.
    1 kilometer 8 meters = 1000 meters + 8 meters
    = 1008 meters
    Ratio = 1008 : 672
    Divide both terms by 336.
    1008 ÷ 336 = 3
    672 ÷ 336 = 2
    Answer: 3 : 2
  • Q: Q1(v). Find the ratio between the following quantities and reduce them to the lowest form: 2 hours, 8 minute and 3 hours, 12 minutes.
    Ans: Method: First change both quantities to the same unit (minutes), then reduce the ratio by the HCF.
    2 hours 8 minutes = 2 × 60 + 8 = 128 minutes
    3 hours 12 minutes = 3 × 60 + 12 = 192 minutes
    Ratio = 128 : 192
    Divide both terms by 64.
    128 ÷ 64 = 2
    192 ÷ 64 = 3
    Answer: 2 : 3
  • Q: Q2(i). Convert the ratio to its lowest form: 25 : 35
    Ans: Method: Divide both terms of the ratio by their HCF.
    HCF of 25 and 35 is 5.
    25 ÷ 5 = 5
    35 ÷ 5 = 7
    Answer: 5 : 7
  • Q: Q2(ii). Convert the ratio to its lowest form: 28 : 84
    Ans: Method: Divide both terms of the ratio by their HCF.
    HCF of 28 and 84 is 28.
    28 ÷ 28 = 1
    84 ÷ 28 = 3
    Answer: 1 : 3
  • Q: Q2(iii). Convert the ratio to its lowest form: 40 : 24
    Ans: Method: Divide both terms of the ratio by their HCF.
    HCF of 40 and 24 is 8.
    40 ÷ 8 = 5
    24 ÷ 8 = 3
    Answer: 5 : 3
  • Q: Q2(iv). Convert the ratio to its lowest form: 200 : 150
    Ans: Method: Divide both terms of the ratio by their HCF.
    HCF of 200 and 150 is 50.
    200 ÷ 50 = 4
    150 ÷ 50 = 3
    Answer: 4 : 3
  • Q: Q2(v). Convert the ratio to its lowest form: 0.45 : 0.75
    Ans: Method: Multiply both terms by 100 to remove the decimals, then divide by the HCF.
    0.45 : 0.75 = 45 : 75
    HCF of 45 and 75 is 15.
    45 ÷ 15 = 3
    75 ÷ 15 = 5
    Answer: 3 : 5
  • Q: Q3. The age of Uzair is 10 years, 8 months and the age of Usman is 13 years, 4 months. Find the ratio between their ages in the lowest form.
    Ans: Method: Change both ages to months, then reduce the ratio by the HCF.
    Age of Uzair = 10 × 12 + 8 = 128 months
    Age of Usman = 13 × 12 + 4 = 160 months
    Ratio = 128 : 160
    Divide both terms by 32.
    128 ÷ 32 = 4
    160 ÷ 32 = 5
    Answer: 4 : 5
  • Q: Q4. Weekly income of a labour is Rs.1500, and of a carpenter Rs.2000 per week. Find the ratio between their weekly incomes in the lowest form.
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio of the incomes and divide both terms by their HCF.
    Ratio = 1500 : 2000
    Divide both terms by 500.
    1500 ÷ 500 = 3
    2000 ÷ 500 = 4
    Answer: 3 : 4
  • Q: Q5. Saeeda earns Rs.85,000 and spends Rs.51,000 in a year. Find the ratio of her income to expenditure.
    Ans: Method: Write income : expenditure and divide both terms by their HCF.
    Ratio = 85000 : 51000
    Divide both terms by 17000.
    85000 ÷ 17000 = 5
    51000 ÷ 17000 = 3
    Answer: 5 : 3
  • Q: Q6. A car covered 360 km in 4 hours, and another car covered 240 km in 4 hours. Find the ratio between the distances covered by both the cars.
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio of the distances and divide both terms by their HCF.
    Ratio = 360 : 240
    Divide both terms by 120.
    360 ÷ 120 = 3
    240 ÷ 120 = 2
    Answer: 3 : 2
  • Q: Q7. In a 100 meter race Zahid covered it in 5.8 minutes, while Iqbal covered it in 4.8 minutes. Find the ratio between their timing.
    Ans: Method: Write the ratio of the timings, multiply by 10 to remove the decimals, then reduce by the HCF.
    Ratio = 5.8 : 4.8
    = 58 : 48
    Divide both terms by 2.
    58 ÷ 2 = 29
    48 ÷ 2 = 24
    Answer: 29 : 24
  • Q: Q8. In an examination 112 students appeared. Out of them 16 failed. Find the ratio between the passed and failed students.
    Ans: Method: First find the number of passed students, then write passed : failed and reduce.
    Total students = 112
    Failed students = 16
    Passed students = 112 − 16 = 96
    Ratio = 96 : 16
    Divide both terms by 16.
    96 ÷ 16 = 6
    16 ÷ 16 = 1
    Answer: 6 : 1

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of Rs.450 to Rs.525 in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio as 450 : 525. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 75. Step 3: 450 ÷ 75 = 6. Step 4: 525 ÷ 75 = 7. So the lowest form is 6 : 7.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of 364 cows to 455 cows in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio as 364 : 455. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 91. Step 3: 364 ÷ 91 = 4. Step 4: 455 ÷ 91 = 5. So the lowest form is 4 : 5.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of 594 kg to 990 kg in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio as 594 : 990. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 198. Step 3: 594 ÷ 198 = 3. Step 4: 990 ÷ 198 = 5. So the lowest form is 3 : 5.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of 1 kilometer 8 meters to 672 meters in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Change both quantities to the same unit: 1 kilometer 8 meters = 1000 + 8 = 1008 meters. Step 2: Ratio = 1008 : 672. Step 3: Divide both terms by 336: 1008 ÷ 336 = 3 and 672 ÷ 336 = 2. So the lowest form is 3 : 2.

mcqs.q: What is the ratio of 2 hours 8 minutes to 3 hours 12 minutes in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Change both times to minutes: 2 × 60 + 8 = 128 minutes and 3 × 60 + 12 = 192 minutes. Step 2: Ratio = 128 : 192. Step 3: Divide both terms by 64: 128 ÷ 64 = 2 and 192 ÷ 64 = 3. So the lowest form is 2 : 3.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of the ratio 28 : 84?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the HCF of 28 and 84, which is 28. Step 2: Divide both terms by 28: 28 ÷ 28 = 1. Step 3: 84 ÷ 28 = 3. So the lowest form is 1 : 3.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of the ratio 40 : 24?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the HCF of 40 and 24, which is 8. Step 2: Divide both terms by 8: 40 ÷ 8 = 5. Step 3: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. So the lowest form is 5 : 3.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of the ratio 200 : 150?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the HCF of 200 and 150, which is 50. Step 2: Divide both terms by 50: 200 ÷ 50 = 4. Step 3: 150 ÷ 50 = 3. So the lowest form is 4 : 3.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of the ratio 0.45 : 0.75?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply both terms by 100 to remove the decimals: 0.45 : 0.75 = 45 : 75. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 15: 45 ÷ 15 = 3. Step 3: 75 ÷ 15 = 5. So the lowest form is 3 : 5.

mcqs.q: Uzair is 10 years 8 months old and Usman is 13 years 4 months old. What is the ratio of Uzair's age to Usman's age in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Change both ages to months: Uzair = 10 × 12 + 8 = 128 months; Usman = 13 × 12 + 4 = 160 months. Step 2: Ratio = 128 : 160. Step 3: Divide both terms by 32: 128 ÷ 32 = 4 and 160 ÷ 32 = 5. So the ratio is 4 : 5.

mcqs.q: A labourer earns Rs.1500 per week and a carpenter earns Rs.2000 per week. What is the ratio of the labourer's weekly income to the carpenter's weekly income in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio of the incomes as 1500 : 2000. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 500. Step 3: 1500 ÷ 500 = 3. Step 4: 2000 ÷ 500 = 4. So the ratio is 3 : 4.

mcqs.q: Saeeda earns Rs.85,000 in a year and spends Rs.51,000. What is the ratio of her income to her expenditure?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write income : expenditure = 85000 : 51000. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 17000. Step 3: 85000 ÷ 17000 = 5. Step 4: 51000 ÷ 17000 = 3. So the ratio is 5 : 3.

mcqs.q: One car covered 360 km in 4 hours and another car covered 240 km in 4 hours. What is the ratio of the distance covered by the first car to the distance covered by the second car?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio of the distances as 360 : 240. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 120. Step 3: 360 ÷ 120 = 3. Step 4: 240 ÷ 120 = 2. So the ratio is 3 : 2.

mcqs.q: In a 100 meter race, Zahid took 5.8 minutes and Iqbal took 4.8 minutes. What is the ratio of Zahid's timing to Iqbal's timing in its lowest form?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio of the timings as 5.8 : 4.8. Step 2: Multiply both terms by 10 to remove the decimals: 58 : 48. Step 3: Divide both terms by 2: 58 ÷ 2 = 29 and 48 ÷ 2 = 24. So the ratio is 29 : 24.

mcqs.q: In an examination, 112 students appeared and 16 failed. What is the ratio of the passed students to the failed students?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the passed students: passed = total − failed = 112 − 16 = 96. Step 2: Ratio = passed : failed = 96 : 16. Step 3: Divide both terms by 16: 96 ÷ 16 = 6 and 16 ÷ 16 = 1. So the ratio is 6 : 1.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A proportion is true only when the product of the extremes equals the product of the means.
  • To find a missing term in a proportion, set product of extremes = product of means and then divide.
  • A relation of the form y = kx is direct proportion; a relation of the form y = k/x is inverse proportion.
  • Unitary method: first find the value for one unit (one chair, one banana, Rs.1), then multiply by the number required.

Exercise 6.2

  • Q: Q1(i). Which of the following proportions are true? 5/3 = 20/12
    Ans: Method: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means.
    Write as 5 : 3 :: 20 : 12
    Product of extremes = 5 × 12 = 60
    Product of means = 3 × 20 = 60
    Both products are equal.
    Answer: True
  • Q: Q1(ii). Which of the following proportions are true? 11/13 = 55/65
    Ans: Method: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means.
    Write as 11 : 13 :: 55 : 65
    Product of extremes = 11 × 65 = 715
    Product of means = 13 × 55 = 715
    Both products are equal.
    Answer: True
  • Q: Q1(iii). Which of the following proportions are true? 11/13 = 44/65
    Ans: Method: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means.
    Write as 11 : 13 :: 44 : 65
    Product of extremes = 11 × 65 = 715
    Product of means = 13 × 44 = 572
    715 ≠ 572, so the products are not equal.
    Answer: Not true (False)
  • Q: Q1(iv). Which of the following proportions are true? 12 : 6 :: 24 : 12
    Ans: Method: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are 12 and 12, means are 6 and 24.
    Product of extremes = 12 × 12 = 144
    Product of means = 6 × 24 = 144
    Both products are equal.
    Answer: True
  • Q: Q1(v). Which of the following proportions are true? 6 : 2 :: 18 : 4
    Ans: Method: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are 6 and 4, means are 2 and 18.
    Product of extremes = 6 × 4 = 24
    Product of means = 2 × 18 = 36
    24 ≠ 36, so the products are not equal.
    Answer: Not true (False)
  • Q: Q2(i). Find the value of □ in the following proportion: 5 : 3 :: □ : 12
    Ans: Method: Product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are 5 and 12, means are 3 and □.
    5 × 12 = 3 × □
    60 = 3 × □
    □ = 60 ÷ 3 = 20
    Answer: □ = 20
  • Q: Q2(ii). Find the value of □ in the following proportion: □ : 13 :: 55 : 65
    Ans: Method: Product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are □ and 65, means are 13 and 55.
    □ × 65 = 13 × 55
    □ × 65 = 715
    □ = 715 ÷ 65 = 11
    Answer: □ = 11
  • Q: Q2(iii). Find the value of □ in the following proportion: 20 : 9 :: 40 : □
    Ans: Method: Product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are 20 and □, means are 9 and 40.
    20 × □ = 9 × 40
    20 × □ = 360
    □ = 360 ÷ 20 = 18
    Answer: □ = 18
  • Q: Q2(iv). Find the value of □ in the following proportion: 22 : □ :: 44 : 52
    Ans: Method: Product of extremes = product of means.
    Extremes are 22 and 52, means are □ and 44.
    22 × 52 = □ × 44
    1144 = □ × 44
    □ = 1144 ÷ 44 = 26
    Answer: □ = 26
  • MCQ: Q3. Anwar is standing next to a flagpole as shown in the figure. Anwar is 6 feet tall, his shadow is 3 ft long and the shadow of the flagpole is 12 ft long. Which proportion could you use to find the height x of the flagpole?
    (a) 3/6 = x/12   (b) x/6 = 3/12   (c) 6/3 = x/12   (d) 3/x = 12/6
    Correct answer: 6/3 = x/12
  • Q: Q4(i). Test which of the following relations are in direct proportion and which are inversely proportional: y = 3x
    Ans: Method: A relation of the form y = kx (k constant) is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion.
    y = 3x is of the form y = kx, with k = 3.
    As x increases, y also increases in the same ratio.
    Answer: Direct proportion
  • Q: Q4(ii). Test which of the following relations are in direct proportion and which are inversely proportional: y = 2/(3x)
    Ans: Method: A relation of the form y = kx is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion.
    y = 2/(3x) can be written as y = (2/3) × (1/x), of the form y = k/x, with k = 2/3.
    As x increases, y decreases in the same ratio.
    Answer: Inverse proportion
  • Q: Q4(iii). Test which of the following relations are in direct proportion and which are inversely proportional: y = 4x
    Ans: Method: A relation of the form y = kx (k constant) is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion.
    y = 4x is of the form y = kx, with k = 4.
    As x increases, y also increases in the same ratio.
    Answer: Direct proportion
  • Q: Q4(iv). Test which of the following relations are in direct proportion and which are inversely proportional: y = 7/x
    Ans: Method: A relation of the form y = kx is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion.
    y = 7/x is of the form y = k/x, with k = 7.
    As x increases, y decreases in the same ratio.
    Answer: Inverse proportion
  • Q: Q5. Price of 5 chairs is Rs.400. Find the price of 15 chairs.
    Ans: Method: Unitary method — first find the price of 1 chair, then multiply by 15.
    Price of 5 chairs = Rs.400
    Price of 1 chair = 400 ÷ 5 = Rs.80
    Price of 15 chairs = 80 × 15
    = Rs.1200
    Answer: Rs.1200
  • Q: Q6. Price of one dozen of bananas is Rs.30. Find the price of 100 bananas.
    Ans: Method: Unitary method — one dozen = 12 bananas; first find the price of 1 banana, then multiply by 100.
    Price of 12 bananas = Rs.30
    Price of 1 banana = 30 ÷ 12 = Rs.2.50
    Price of 100 bananas = 2.50 × 100
    = Rs.250
    Answer: Rs.250
  • Q: Q7. A shopkeeper earned a profit of Rs.27 on selling goods for Rs.360. Find the profit on selling goods for Rs.100.
    Ans: Method: Unitary method — first find the profit on goods of Rs.1, then multiply by 100.
    On goods of Rs.360, profit = Rs.27
    On goods of Rs.1, profit = 27 ÷ 360 = Rs.0.075
    On goods of Rs.100, profit = 0.075 × 100
    = Rs.7.50
    Answer: Rs.7.50
  • Q: Q8. Majida paid Zakat of Rs.25 on Rs.1000. How much Zakat Farida will pay on Rs.8000.
    Ans: Method: Unitary method — first find the Zakat on Rs.1, then multiply by 8000.
    On Rs.1000, Zakat = Rs.25
    On Rs.1, Zakat = 25 ÷ 1000 = Rs.0.025
    On Rs.8000, Zakat = 0.025 × 8000
    = Rs.200
    Answer: Rs.200

mcqs.q: Is the proportion 5/3 = 20/12 true?
options: False, because 20/12 is not in lowest form
mcqs.why: Rule: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: Write 5 : 3 :: 20 : 12. Step 2: Product of extremes = 5 × 12 = 60. Step 3: Product of means = 3 × 20 = 60. Step 4: Both products are equal, so the proportion is true.

mcqs.q: Is the proportion 11/13 = 44/65 true?
options: False, because 65 is not a multiple of 13
mcqs.why: Rule: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: Write 11 : 13 :: 44 : 65. Step 2: Product of extremes = 11 × 65 = 715. Step 3: Product of means = 13 × 44 = 572. Step 4: 715 ≠ 572, so the products are not equal and the proportion is not true.

mcqs.q: Is the proportion 6 : 2 :: 18 : 4 true?
options: True, because both ratios have even numbers
mcqs.why: Rule: In a true proportion, product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: The extremes are 6 and 4, and the means are 2 and 18. Step 2: Product of extremes = 6 × 4 = 24. Step 3: Product of means = 2 × 18 = 36. Step 4: 24 ≠ 36, so the proportion is not true.

mcqs.q: Find the missing term: 5 : 3 :: □ : 12
mcqs.why: Rule: Product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: The extremes are 5 and 12, and the means are 3 and □. Step 2: 5 × 12 = 3 × □. Step 3: 60 = 3 × □. Step 4: □ = 60 ÷ 3 = 20.

mcqs.q: Find the missing term: □ : 13 :: 55 : 65
mcqs.why: Rule: Product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: The extremes are □ and 65, and the means are 13 and 55. Step 2: □ × 65 = 13 × 55. Step 3: □ × 65 = 715. Step 4: □ = 715 ÷ 65 = 11.

mcqs.q: Find the missing term: 20 : 9 :: 40 : □
mcqs.why: Rule: Product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: The extremes are 20 and □, and the means are 9 and 40. Step 2: 20 × □ = 9 × 40. Step 3: 20 × □ = 360. Step 4: □ = 360 ÷ 20 = 18.

mcqs.q: Find the missing term: 22 : □ :: 44 : 52
mcqs.why: Rule: Product of extremes = product of means. Step 1: The extremes are 22 and 52, and the means are □ and 44. Step 2: 22 × 52 = □ × 44. Step 3: 1144 = □ × 44. Step 4: □ = 1144 ÷ 44 = 26.

mcqs.q: Anwar is 6 feet tall, his shadow is 3 ft long and the shadow of a flagpole is 12 ft long. Which proportion could you use to find the height x of the flagpole?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Match each height with its own shadow: Anwar's height 6 ft goes with his shadow 3 ft, and the flagpole's height x goes with its shadow 12 ft. Step 2: Height ÷ shadow must be the same for both: 6/3 = x/12. Step 3: Check: product of extremes = product of means gives 6 × 12 = 3 × x, so x = 72 ÷ 3 = 24 ft.

mcqs.q: Which kind of proportion is shown by the relation y = 3x?
mcqs.why: Rule: A relation of the form y = kx (k constant) is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion. Step 1: y = 3x is of the form y = kx with k = 3. Step 2: As x increases, y also increases in the same ratio. So it is direct proportion.

mcqs.q: Which kind of proportion is shown by the relation y = 2/(3x)?
mcqs.why: Rule: A relation of the form y = kx is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion. Step 1: y = 2/(3x) can be written as y = (2/3) × (1/x). Step 2: This is of the form y = k/x with k = 2/3. Step 3: As x increases, y decreases in the same ratio. So it is inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: Which kind of proportion is shown by the relation y = 7/x?
mcqs.why: Rule: A relation of the form y = kx is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion. Step 1: y = 7/x is of the form y = k/x with k = 7. Step 2: As x increases, y decreases in the same ratio. So it is inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: The price of 5 chairs is Rs.400. What is the price of 15 chairs?
mcqs.why: Unitary method. Step 1: Price of 5 chairs = Rs.400. Step 2: Price of 1 chair = 400 ÷ 5 = Rs.80. Step 3: Price of 15 chairs = 80 × 15 = Rs.1200.

mcqs.q: The price of one dozen bananas is Rs.30. What is the price of 100 bananas?
mcqs.why: Unitary method. Step 1: One dozen = 12 bananas, and the price of 12 bananas = Rs.30. Step 2: Price of 1 banana = 30 ÷ 12 = Rs.2.50. Step 3: Price of 100 bananas = 2.50 × 100 = Rs.250.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper earned a profit of Rs.27 on selling goods for Rs.360. What is the profit on selling goods for Rs.100?
mcqs.why: Unitary method. Step 1: On goods of Rs.360, profit = Rs.27. Step 2: On goods of Rs.1, profit = 27 ÷ 360 = Rs.0.075. Step 3: On goods of Rs.100, profit = 0.075 × 100 = Rs.7.50.

mcqs.q: Majida paid Zakat of Rs.25 on Rs.1000. How much Zakat will Farida pay on Rs.8000?
mcqs.why: Unitary method. Step 1: On Rs.1000, Zakat = Rs.25. Step 2: On Rs.1, Zakat = 25 ÷ 1000 = Rs.0.025. Step 3: On Rs.8000, Zakat = 0.025 × 8000 = Rs.200.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In a ratio, the first term is the antecedent and the second term is the consequent.
  • In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the outer terms a and d are the extremes and the inner terms b and c are the means.
  • Ratios and fractions are put in lowest form by dividing both terms by their HCF; decimals are cleared first by multiplying by 10 or 100.
  • Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + width), so the length can be found from the perimeter and the width before forming a ratio.
  • In inverse proportion problems such as food for persons, the total (persons × days) stays the same, so fewer persons means more days.

Review Exercise 6

  • Fill in the blank: Q1(i). The numbers 27 and 9 are in the ratio 3 : 1
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(ii). The number 2.7 and 0.9 are in the ratio 3 : 1
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(iii). The numbers 3/2 and 7/2 are in the ratio of 3 : 7
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(iv). In 3 : 5, antecedent = 3 and consequent = 5
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(v). In 13.5 : 17.2, antecedent = 13.5 and consequent = 17.2
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(vi). The lowest form of 9/12 = 3/4
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(vii). The lowest form of 4.5/1.5 = 3/1 = 3
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(viii). The lowest form of 65 : 39 = 5 : 3
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(ix). In 1 : 2 :: 2 : 4, extremes are 1 and 4 and means are 2 and 2
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(x). In 3.2 : 5 :: 6.4 : 10, extremes are 3.2 and 10 and means are 5 and 6.4
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(xi). y = (1/2)x is in direct proportion
  • Fill in the blank: Q1(xii). y = 7x is in direct proportion
  • Q: Q2. The perimeter of a farm is 187.2 m. If its width is 39m, then find the ratio between its length and width.
    Ans: Method: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + width). First find the length, then write length : width and reduce.
    2 × (length + 39) = 187.2
    length + 39 = 187.2 ÷ 2 = 93.6
    length = 93.6 − 39 = 54.6 m
    Ratio = 54.6 : 39
    Multiply both terms by 10: 546 : 390
    Divide both terms by 78.
    546 ÷ 78 = 7
    390 ÷ 78 = 5
    Answer: 7 : 5
  • Q: Q3. Sum of the heights of Bushra and Sajida is 3.3m. If the height of Sajida is 1.5 m, find the ratio between their heights.
    Ans: Method: First find the height of Bushra, then write the ratio of their heights and reduce.
    Height of Sajida = 1.5 m
    Height of Bushra = 3.3 − 1.5 = 1.8 m
    Ratio (Bushra : Sajida) = 1.8 : 1.5
    Multiply both terms by 10: 18 : 15
    Divide both terms by 3.
    18 ÷ 3 = 6
    15 ÷ 3 = 5
    Answer: 6 : 5
  • Q: Q4. Price of 3 kg of apples is Rs.135. Find the price of 11kg of apples.
    Ans: Method: Unitary method — first find the price of 1 kg, then multiply by 11.
    Price of 3 kg apples = Rs.135
    Price of 1 kg apples = 135 ÷ 3 = Rs.45
    Price of 11 kg apples = 45 × 11
    = Rs.495
    Answer: Rs.495
  • Q: Q5. In a house of 15 persons food was sufficient for 30 days. 5 persons left the house. For how many days the food would be sufficient?
    Ans: Method: This is inverse proportion — fewer persons, the food lasts for more days. Total food = persons × days.
    Persons left in the house = 15 − 5 = 10
    Total food = 15 × 30 = 450 person-days
    Number of days for 10 persons = 450 ÷ 10
    = 45 days
    Answer: 45 days

mcqs.q: The numbers 27 and 9 are in the ratio:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write the ratio as 27 : 9. Step 2: Divide both terms by their HCF, 9: 27 ÷ 9 = 3. Step 3: 9 ÷ 9 = 1. So the numbers are in the ratio 3 : 1.

mcqs.q: The numbers 2.7 and 0.9 are in the ratio:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply both numbers by 10 to remove the decimals: 2.7 and 0.9 become 27 and 9. Step 2: Ratio = 27 : 9. Step 3: Divide both terms by 9: 27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 9 ÷ 9 = 1. So the ratio is 3 : 1.

mcqs.q: The numbers 3/2 and 7/2 are in the ratio:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Both fractions have the same denominator 2, so compare the numerators 3 and 7. Step 2: (3/2) ÷ (7/2) = 3/7. So the numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7.

mcqs.q: In the ratio 3 : 5, what are the antecedent and the consequent?
mcqs.why: Rule: In a ratio, the first term is called the antecedent and the second term is called the consequent. Step 1: In 3 : 5 the first term is 3. Step 2: The second term is 5. So antecedent = 3 and consequent = 5.

mcqs.q: In the ratio 13.5 : 17.2, what are the antecedent and the consequent?
mcqs.why: Rule: In a ratio, the first term is called the antecedent and the second term is called the consequent. Step 1: In 13.5 : 17.2 the first term is 13.5. Step 2: The second term is 17.2. So antecedent = 13.5 and consequent = 17.2.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of 9/12?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the HCF of 9 and 12, which is 3. Step 2: Divide the numerator by 3: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Step 3: Divide the denominator by 3: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. So the lowest form of 9/12 is 3/4.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of 4.5/1.5?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Multiply numerator and denominator by 10 to remove the decimals: 4.5/1.5 = 45/15. Step 2: Divide both by their HCF, 15: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 and 15 ÷ 15 = 1. So the lowest form is 3/1 = 3.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest form of the ratio 65 : 39?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the HCF of 65 and 39, which is 13. Step 2: Divide both terms by 13: 65 ÷ 13 = 5. Step 3: 39 ÷ 13 = 3. So the lowest form is 5 : 3.

mcqs.q: In 1 : 2 :: 2 : 4, what are the extremes and the means?
options: Extremes are 2 and 2; means are 1 and 4
Extremes are 1 and 2; means are 2 and 4
Extremes are 1 and 4; means are 2 and 2
Extremes are 4 and 2; means are 1 and 2
mcqs.why: Rule: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the outer terms (a and d) are the extremes and the inner terms (b and c) are the means. Step 1: In 1 : 2 :: 2 : 4 the outer terms are 1 and 4. Step 2: The inner terms are 2 and 2. So extremes are 1 and 4, and means are 2 and 2.

mcqs.q: In 3.2 : 5 :: 6.4 : 10, what are the extremes and the means?
options: Extremes are 5 and 6.4; means are 3.2 and 10
Extremes are 3.2 and 10; means are 5 and 6.4
Extremes are 3.2 and 5; means are 6.4 and 10
Extremes are 10 and 5; means are 3.2 and 6.4
mcqs.why: Rule: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the outer terms (a and d) are the extremes and the inner terms (b and c) are the means. Step 1: In 3.2 : 5 :: 6.4 : 10 the outer terms are 3.2 and 10. Step 2: The inner terms are 5 and 6.4. So extremes are 3.2 and 10, and means are 5 and 6.4.

mcqs.q: The relation y = (1/2)x is in which kind of proportion?
mcqs.why: Rule: A relation of the form y = kx (k constant) is direct proportion, and y = k/x is inverse proportion. Step 1: y = (1/2)x is of the form y = kx with k = 1/2. Step 2: As x increases, y increases in the same ratio. So it is direct proportion.

mcqs.q: The perimeter of a farm is 187.2 m and its width is 39 m. What is the ratio of its length to its width?
mcqs.why: Formula: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + width). Step 1: 2 × (length + 39) = 187.2, so length + 39 = 187.2 ÷ 2 = 93.6. Step 2: Length = 93.6 − 39 = 54.6 m. Step 3: Ratio = 54.6 : 39 = 546 : 390. Step 4: Divide both terms by 78: 546 ÷ 78 = 7 and 390 ÷ 78 = 5. So the ratio is 7 : 5.

mcqs.q: The sum of the heights of Bushra and Sajida is 3.3 m. Sajida's height is 1.5 m. What is the ratio of Bushra's height to Sajida's height?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find Bushra's height: 3.3 − 1.5 = 1.8 m. Step 2: Ratio (Bushra : Sajida) = 1.8 : 1.5. Step 3: Multiply both terms by 10: 18 : 15. Step 4: Divide both terms by 3: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 and 15 ÷ 3 = 5. So the ratio is 6 : 5.

mcqs.q: The price of 3 kg of apples is Rs.135. What is the price of 11 kg of apples?
mcqs.why: Unitary method. Step 1: Price of 3 kg of apples = Rs.135. Step 2: Price of 1 kg of apples = 135 ÷ 3 = Rs.45. Step 3: Price of 11 kg of apples = 45 × 11 = Rs.495.

mcqs.q: In a house of 15 persons, food was sufficient for 30 days. If 5 persons left the house, for how many days will the food now be sufficient?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion: fewer persons, so the food lasts for more days. Step 1: Persons left in the house = 15 − 5 = 10. Step 2: Total food = persons × days = 15 × 30 = 450 person-days. Step 3: Number of days for 10 persons = 450 ÷ 10 = 45 days.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 — Part 1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce to the lowest form.
  • For a mixed-number percent, first change it into an improper fraction, then multiply by 1/100 and reduce.
  • To convert a fraction into a percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
  • A percent greater than 100% gives a fraction greater than 1, e.g. 2 1/4 = 225%.

Exercise 7.1 (Questions 1–11)

  • Q: Q1(i). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 80%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce to the lowest form.
    80% = 80 × (1/100) = 80/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 20.
    80/100 = 4/5
    Answer: 4/5
  • Q: Q1(ii). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 60%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce to the lowest form.
    60% = 60 × (1/100) = 60/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 20.
    60/100 = 3/5
    Answer: 3/5
  • Q: Q1(iii). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 12 1/2%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, first write the mixed number as an improper fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce.
    12 1/2% = 25/2 × (1/100)
    = 25/200
    Divide numerator and denominator by 25.
    25/200 = 1/8
    Answer: 1/8
  • Q: Q1(iv). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 16 2/3%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, first write the mixed number as an improper fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce.
    16 2/3% = 50/3 × (1/100)
    = 50/300
    Divide numerator and denominator by 50.
    50/300 = 1/6
    Answer: 1/6
  • Q: Q1(v). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 13%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce to the lowest form.
    13% = 13 × (1/100) = 13/100
    13 and 100 have no common factor, so it is already in the lowest form.
    Answer: 13/100
  • Q: Q1(vi). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 10%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce to the lowest form.
    10% = 10 × (1/100) = 10/100
    Divide numerator and denominator by 10.
    10/100 = 1/10
    Answer: 1/10
  • Q: Q1(vii). Convert each of the following percent into lowest common fraction: 12 2/3%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a fraction, first write the mixed number as an improper fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce.
    12 2/3% = 38/3 × (1/100)
    = 38/300
    Divide numerator and denominator by 2.
    38/300 = 19/150
    Answer: 19/150
  • Q: Q2(i). Convert the following as percent: 9/15
    Ans: Method: To convert a fraction into percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
    9/15 × 100% = (9 × 100)/15 %
    = 900/15 %
    = 60%
    Answer: 60%
  • Q: Q2(ii). Convert the following as percent: 7/30
    Ans: Method: To convert a fraction into percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
    7/30 × 100% = (7 × 100)/30 %
    = 70/3 %
    = 23 1/3%
    Answer: 23 1/3%
  • Q: Q2(iii). Convert the following as percent: 2 1/4
    Ans: Method: To convert a fraction into percent, first write the mixed number as an improper fraction, then multiply by 100%.
    2 1/4 = 9/4
    9/4 × 100% = (9 × 100)/4 %
    = 900/4 %
    = 225%
    Answer: 225%
  • Q: Q2(iv). Convert the following as percent: 1/16
    Ans: Method: To convert a fraction into percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
    1/16 × 100% = 100/16 %
    = 25/4 %
    = 6 1/4%
    Answer: 6 1/4%

mcqs.q: Convert 80% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100. 80% = 80 x (1/100) = 80/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 20: 80/100 = 4/5, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: 60% written as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100. 60% = 60 x (1/100) = 60/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 20: 60/100 = 3/5, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Convert 12 1/2% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: First write the mixed number as an improper fraction: 12 1/2 = 25/2. Then replace the % sign by 1/100: 12 1/2% = 25/2 x (1/100) = 25/200. Divide the numerator and denominator by 25: 25/200 = 1/8.

mcqs.q: 16 2/3% as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: First write the mixed number as an improper fraction: 16 2/3 = 50/3. Then replace the % sign by 1/100: 16 2/3% = 50/3 x (1/100) = 50/300. Divide the numerator and denominator by 50: 50/300 = 1/6.

mcqs.q: Convert 13% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100. 13% = 13 x (1/100) = 13/100. 13 and 100 have no common factor, so 13/100 is already in the lowest form.

mcqs.q: 10% written as a fraction in its lowest form is:
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100. 10% = 10 x (1/100) = 10/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 10: 10/100 = 1/10, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Convert 12 2/3% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: First write the mixed number as an improper fraction: 12 2/3 = 38/3. Then replace the % sign by 1/100: 12 2/3% = 38/3 x (1/100) = 38/300. Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 38/300 = 19/150, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Convert the fraction 9/15 into a percent.
mcqs.why: To convert a fraction into a percent, multiply the fraction by 100%. Percentage = (Part/Whole) x 100, so 9/15 x 100% = (9 x 100)/15 % = 900/15 % = 60%.

mcqs.q: The fraction 7/30 expressed as a percent is:
mcqs.why: To convert a fraction into a percent, multiply the fraction by 100%. 7/30 x 100% = (7 x 100)/30 % = 70/3 % = 23 1/3%.

mcqs.q: Convert 2 1/4 into a percent.
mcqs.why: First write the mixed number as an improper fraction: 2 1/4 = 9/4. Then multiply by 100%: 9/4 x 100% = (9 x 100)/4 % = 900/4 % = 225%.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 — Part 2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To convert a fraction into a percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
  • To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, remove the % sign and divide by 100 — move the decimal point two places to the left.
  • To convert a decimal fraction into a percent, multiply by 100% — move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign.
  • A percent above 100% becomes a decimal greater than 1, e.g. 125% = 1.25.

Exercise 7.1 (Questions 12–22)

  • Q: Q2(v). Convert the following as percent: 8/25
    Ans: Method: To convert a fraction into percent, multiply the fraction by 100%.
    8/25 × 100% = (8 × 100)/25 %
    = 800/25 %
    = 32%
    Answer: 32%
  • Q: Q3(i). Express each of the following as decimal fraction: 40%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, remove the % sign and move the decimal point two places to the left (divide by 100).
    40% = 40/100
    = 0.40
    Answer: 0.4
  • Q: Q3(ii). Express each of the following as decimal fraction: 75%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, remove the % sign and move the decimal point two places to the left (divide by 100).
    75% = 75/100
    = 0.75
    Answer: 0.75
  • Q: Q3(iii). Express each of the following as decimal fraction: 125%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, remove the % sign and move the decimal point two places to the left (divide by 100).
    125% = 125/100
    = 1.25
    Answer: 1.25
  • Q: Q3(iv). Express each of the following as decimal fraction: 0.4%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, remove the % sign and move the decimal point two places to the left (divide by 100).
    0.4% = 0.4/100
    = 0.004
    Answer: 0.004
  • Q: Q3(v). Express each of the following as decimal fraction: 33 1/3%
    Ans: Method: To convert a percent into a decimal fraction, first write the mixed number as an improper fraction, then divide by 100.
    33 1/3% = 100/3 %
    = (100/3) ÷ 100 = 100/300
    = 1/3
    = 0.333...
    Answer: 1/3, i.e. about 0.33
  • Q: Q4(i). Convert each of the following decimal fraction into percent: 0.5
    Ans: Method: To convert a decimal fraction into percent, move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign (multiply by 100%).
    0.5 × 100% = 50%
    Answer: 50%
  • Q: Q4(ii). Convert each of the following decimal fraction into percent: 0.76
    Ans: Method: To convert a decimal fraction into percent, move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign (multiply by 100%).
    0.76 × 100% = 76%
    Answer: 76%
  • Q: Q4(iii). Convert each of the following decimal fraction into percent: 2.45
    Ans: Method: To convert a decimal fraction into percent, move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign (multiply by 100%).
    2.45 × 100% = 245%
    Answer: 245%
  • Q: Q4(iv). Convert each of the following decimal fraction into percent: 0.375
    Ans: Method: To convert a decimal fraction into percent, move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign (multiply by 100%).
    0.375 × 100% = 37.5%
    Answer: 37.5%
  • Q: Q4(v). Convert each of the following decimal fraction into percent: 0.0125
    Ans: Method: To convert a decimal fraction into percent, move the decimal point two places to the right and write the % sign (multiply by 100%).
    0.0125 × 100% = 1.25%
    Answer: 1.25%
