lessons.title: Exercises 7.2 and 7.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Percentage = (Part / Whole) x 100; the whole is always 100%, so a remaining part = 100% minus the given parts.
  • Discount = rate of discount x price, and Amount paid = Price - Discount.
  • Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price when S.P > C.P; Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price when S.P < C.P.
  • Profit percent = (Profit / Cost Price) x 100; extra costs like decoration are added to the cost price first.
  • For dozens, first find the total cost price and total selling price for all the dozens, then subtract.

Exercise 7.2

  • Q: Q1. A squared box is divided into 100 equal circles of the same radii. 30 circles are black, 20 are blue and the remaining circles are red. What is the percentage of red circles in the box?
    Ans: Method: Percentage = (part ÷ total) × 100%. First find the number of red circles.
    Total circles = 100
    Black circles = 30
    Blue circles = 20
    Red circles = 100 − 30 − 20 = 50
    Percentage of red circles = 50/100 × 100%
    = 50%
    Answer: 50%
  • Q: Q2. 25% of a wall painted blue, 30% painted green and the rest of the wall painted white. Find the percentage of the white part of the wall.
    Ans: Method: The whole wall is 100%. Subtract the blue and green parts from 100%.
    Blue part = 25%
    Green part = 30%
    Blue + green = 25% + 30% = 55%
    White part = 100% − 55%
    = 45%
    Answer: 45%
  • Q: Q3. In a home examination Ali obtained 350 marks out of 500. Find the percentage of the marks.
    Ans: Method: Percentage of marks = (marks obtained ÷ total marks) × 100%.
    Marks obtained = 350
    Total marks = 500
    Percentage = 350/500 × 100%
    = 35000/500 %
    = 70%
    Answer: 70%
  • Q: Q4. Aslam got Rs.500 as pocket money in a month. He spent Rs.150 on cold drinks, Rs.100 on stationary and saved the rest amount. What percentage of the pocket money he spent on cold drinks?
    Ans: Method: Percentage spent = (amount spent ÷ total pocket money) × 100%.
    Amount spent on cold drinks = Rs.150
    Total pocket money = Rs.500
    Percentage = 150/500 × 100%
    = 15000/500 %
    = 30%
    Answer: 30%
  • Q: Q5. 20 out of 32 members of a football team weigh over 100 kg. What percent of the team weighs over 100 kg?
    Ans: Method: Percentage = (part ÷ total) × 100%.
    Members weighing over 100 kg = 20
    Total members = 32
    Percentage = 20/32 × 100%
    = 2000/32 %
    = 62.5%
    Answer: 62.5%

Exercise 7.3

  • Q: Q1(i). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Radio — Price Rs.500, Discount 10%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Radio = Rs.500
    Discount = 10% of 500 = (10/100) × 500 = Rs.50
    Amount paid = 500 − 50 = Rs.450
    Answer: Discount = Rs.50, Amount paid = Rs.450
  • Q: Q1(ii). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Kettle — Price Rs.200, Discount 5%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Kettle = Rs.200
    Discount = 5% of 200 = (5/100) × 200 = Rs.10
    Amount paid = 200 − 10 = Rs.190
    Answer: Discount = Rs.10, Amount paid = Rs.190
  • Q: Q1(iii). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Record player — Price Rs.800, Discount 25%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Record player = Rs.800
    Discount = 25% of 800 = (25/100) × 800 = Rs.200
    Amount paid = 800 − 200 = Rs.600
    Answer: Discount = Rs.200, Amount paid = Rs.600
  • Q: Q1(iv). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Refrigerator — Price Rs.25000, Discount 20%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Refrigerator = Rs.25000
    Discount = 20% of 25000 = (20/100) × 25000 = Rs.5000
    Amount paid = 25000 − 5000 = Rs.20000
    Answer: Discount = Rs.5000, Amount paid = Rs.20000
  • Q: Q1(v). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Bicycle — Price Rs.6000, Discount 15%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Bicycle = Rs.6000
    Discount = 15% of 6000 = (15/100) × 6000 = Rs.900
    Amount paid = 6000 − 900 = Rs.5100
    Answer: Discount = Rs.900, Amount paid = Rs.5100
  • Q: Q1(vi). Find the value of the discount and the amount actually paid for the following (from the table in the book): Washing machine — Price Rs.8000, Discount 10%
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × price. Amount paid = Price − Discount.
    Price of Washing machine = Rs.8000
    Discount = 10% of 8000 = (10/100) × 8000 = Rs.800
    Amount paid = 8000 − 800 = Rs.7200
    Answer: Discount = Rs.800, Amount paid = Rs.7200
  • Q: Q2. Aslam bought 5 dozens of eggs at the rate of Rs.30 per dozen and sold per dozen at the rate of Rs.40. Find the profit he gained.
    Ans: Method: Profit = S.P − C.P. First find the total cost price and total selling price of 5 dozens of eggs.
    Cost price of 5 dozens = 5 × 30 = Rs.150
    Selling price of 5 dozens = 5 × 40 = Rs.200
    Profit = S.P − C.P
    = 200 − 150
    = Rs.50
    Answer: Profit = Rs.50
  • Q: Q3. Asim bought a bicycle for Rs.2500 and spent Rs.300 on its decoration. He then sold it for Rs.4000. Find profit percent.
    Ans: Method: Profit percent = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100%, where Profit = S.P − C.P and the decoration cost is added to the cost price.
    Total cost price = 2500 + 300 = Rs.2800
    Selling price = Rs.4000
    Profit = 4000 − 2800 = Rs.1200
    Profit percent = (1200/2800) × 100%
    = 120000/2800 %
    = 300/7 % = 42 6/7%
    Answer: 42 6/7%
  • Q: Q4. A chair was purchased for Rs.600 and sold for Rs.575. Find the profit or Loss.
    Ans: Method: If S.P > C.P there is profit = S.P − C.P; if S.P < C.P there is loss = C.P − S.P.
    Cost price = Rs.600
    Selling price = Rs.575
    Here S.P < C.P, so there is a loss.
    Loss = C.P − S.P
    = 600 − 575
    = Rs.25
    Answer: Loss = Rs.25
  • Q: Q5. Saima bought a pack of ten pencils for Rs.20 and sold per pencil for Rs.2.5. Find profit or loss percent.
    Ans: Method: Profit percent = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) × 100%, where Profit = S.P − C.P. First find the total selling price of the 10 pencils.
    Cost price of 10 pencils = Rs.20
    Selling price of 1 pencil = Rs.2.5
    Selling price of 10 pencils = 10 × 2.5 = Rs.25
    Profit = 25 − 20 = Rs.5
    Profit percent = (5/20) × 100%
    = 25%
    Answer: Profit percent = 25%
  • Q: Q6. A book seller bought 5 dozens note books at the rate of Rs.20 per note book and sold at the rate of Rs.300 per dozen. Find profit or loss.
    Ans: Method: Profit = S.P − C.P and Loss = C.P − S.P. First find the total cost price and total selling price of 5 dozens of note books.
    Cost price per note book = Rs.20
    Cost price per dozen = 12 × 20 = Rs.240
    Cost price of 5 dozens = 5 × 240 = Rs.1200
    Selling price of 5 dozens = 5 × 300 = Rs.1500
    Here S.P > C.P, so there is a profit.
    Profit = 1500 − 1200 = Rs.300
    Answer: Profit = Rs.300
  • Q: Q7. Aqeel bought some books from a book stall costing Rs.1000. He got a discount of 10%. Find the amount that he paid.
    Ans: Method: Discount = rate of discount × marked price. Amount paid = Marked Price − Discount.
    Cost of books = Rs.1000
    Discount = 10% of 1000 = (10/100) × 1000 = Rs.100
    Amount paid = 1000 − 100
    = Rs.900
    Answer: Rs.900
  • Q: Q8. If the written price of a toy is Rs.200 and its discounted price is Rs.150, find the rate of discount.
    Ans: Method: Discount = Marked Price − Discounted Price. Rate of discount = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100%.
    Marked (written) price = Rs.200
    Discounted price = Rs.150
    Discount = 200 − 150 = Rs.50
    Rate of discount = (50/200) × 100%
    = 25%
    Answer: 25%

mcqs.q: A bicycle costs Rs.6,000 and a discount of 15% is given. Find the amount actually paid.

mcqs.q: Aslam bought 5 dozens of eggs at Rs.30 per dozen and sold them at Rs.40 per dozen. Find the profit he gained.

mcqs.q: Asim bought a bicycle for Rs.2,500, spent Rs.300 on its decoration, and sold it for Rs.4,000. Find the profit percent.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • 1% = 1/100, and a fraction is converted to a percent by multiplying by 100%, e.g. 2/5 = 40%.
  • A percent is converted to a decimal by dividing by 100, e.g. 50% = 0.5; a decimal is converted to a percent by multiplying by 100%.
  • Profit = Sale Price - Cost Price.
  • Percentage of a number = (percent / 100) x number; to find the whole when a percent of it is given, divide the given part by the percent and multiply by 100.
  • Percentage = (Part / Whole) x 100, and a price reduced by a percent: New Price = Original Price - (rate x Original Price).

Review Exercise 7

  • True or False: Q1(i). 1/100 = 1% — True
  • True or False: Q1(ii). 25% of 60 = 20 — False — 25% of 60 = 15
  • True or False: Q1(iii). 2/5 = 40% — True
  • True or False: Q1(iv). 50% = 0.4 — False — 50% = 0.5
  • True or False: Q1(v). Profit = Sale price − cost price — True
  • MCQ: Q2(i). Choose the correct answer: 25% = _____ (in friction form)
    (a) 1/4   (b) 1/8   (c) 1/6
    Correct answer: 1/4
  • MCQ: Q2(ii). Choose the correct answer: 0.2 = _____ (in percentage form)
    (a) 2%   (b) 20%   (c) 5%
    Correct answer: 20%
  • MCQ: Q2(iii). Choose the correct answer: 30% = _____ (in decimal form)
    (a) 0.03   (b) 0.3   (c) 30
    Correct answer: 0.3
  • Q: Q3(i). Find the unknown: What number is 50% of 150?
    Ans: Method: Percentage of a number = (percent ÷ 100) × number.
    50% of 150 = (50/100) × 150
    = 7500/100
    = 75
    Answer: 75
  • Q: Q3(ii). Find the unknown: 8 is 5% of what number?
    Ans: Method: If 5% of a number is 8, first find 1% of the number, then multiply by 100.
    Let the number be x.
    5% of x = 8
    (5/100) × x = 8
    x = 8 × 100/5
    x = 800/5 = 160
    Answer: 160
  • Q: Q3(iii). Find the unknown: 12 is 35% of what number?
    Ans: Method: If 35% of a number is 12, first find 1% of the number, then multiply by 100.
    Let the number be x.
    35% of x = 12
    (35/100) × x = 12
    x = 12 × 100/35
    x = 1200/35 = 240/7 = 34 2/7
    Answer: 34 2/7 (about 34.29)
  • Q: Q3(iv). Find the unknown: 98 is what percent of 200?
    Ans: Method: Percentage = (part ÷ whole) × 100%.
    Part = 98
    Whole = 200
    Percentage = 98/200 × 100%
    = 9800/200 %
    = 49%
    Answer: 49%
  • Q: Q3(v). Find the unknown: 8 5/9 is what percent of 11?
    Ans: Method: Percentage = (part ÷ whole) × 100%. First write the mixed number as an improper fraction.
    8 5/9 = 77/9
    Percentage = (77/9 ÷ 11) × 100%
    = (77/99) × 100%
    = 7700/99 %
    = 700/9 % = 77 7/9%
    Answer: 77 7/9%
  • Q: Q4. Twenty five out of 150 students failed mathematics in the annual examination. What percent of the whole class failed?
    Ans: Method: Percentage failed = (students failed ÷ total students) × 100%.
    Students failed = 25
    Total students = 150
    Percentage = 25/150 × 100%
    = 2500/150 %
    = 50/3 % = 16 2/3%
    Answer: 16 2/3%
  • Q: Q5. A car costing 240,000 rupees is reduced in price by 10%. Find the new price.
    Ans: Method: Reduction = rate × original price. New price = Original Price − Reduction.
    Original price = Rs.240,000
    Reduction = 10% of 240000 = (10/100) × 240000 = Rs.24,000
    New price = 240000 − 24000
    = Rs.216,000
    Answer: Rs.216,000

mcqs.q: Which statement is true?
mcqs.why: A percent means out of 100, so 1% = 1/100. Checking the statement: 1/100 = 1% is true, because Percentage = (Part/Whole) x 100 gives 1/100 x 100% = 1%.

mcqs.q: 25% of 60 equals:
mcqs.why: Percentage of a number = (percent / 100) x number. 25% of 60 = (25/100) x 60 = 1500/100 = 15. So the claim that 25% of 60 = 20 is false; the correct value is 15.

mcqs.q: Which statement is true?
mcqs.why: To convert a fraction into a percent, multiply by 100%: 2/5 x 100% = (2 x 100)/5 % = 200/5 % = 40%. So 2/5 = 40% is true.

mcqs.q: 50% expressed as a decimal is:
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a decimal, divide by 100: 50% = 50/100 = 0.5. So the claim that 50% = 0.4 is false; the correct value is 0.5.

mcqs.q: Profit is calculated by the formula:
options: Profit = Sale price x Cost price
mcqs.why: Profit = Selling (Sale) Price - Cost Price. When the sale price is greater than the cost price, this difference is the profit, so the statement is true.

mcqs.q: 25% = _____ (in fraction form)
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a fraction, replace the % sign by 1/100 and reduce: 25% = 25/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 25: 25/100 = 1/4. (This is the book's question; a fourth option has been added.)

mcqs.q: 0.2 = _____ (in percentage form)
mcqs.why: To convert a decimal into a percent, multiply by 100%: 0.2 x 100% = 20%. (This is the book's question; a fourth option has been added.)

mcqs.q: 30% = _____ (in decimal form)
mcqs.why: To convert a percent into a decimal, divide by 100: 30% = 30/100 = 0.3. (This is the book's question; a fourth option has been added.)

mcqs.q: What number is 50% of 150?
mcqs.why: Percentage of a number = (percent / 100) x number. 50% of 150 = (50/100) x 150 = 7500/100 = 75.

mcqs.q: 8 is 5% of what number?
mcqs.why: Let the number be x. 5% of x = 8, so (5/100) x x = 8. Then x = 8 x 100/5 = 800/5 = 160.

mcqs.q: 12 is 35% of what number?
98 is what percent of 200?
8 5/9 is what percent of 11?
mcqs.why: First write the mixed number as an improper fraction: 8 5/9 = 77/9. Percentage = (Part / Whole) x 100 = (77/9 / 11) x 100% = (77/99) x 100% = 7700/99 % = 700/9 % = 77 7/9%.

mcqs.q: Twenty five out of 150 students failed mathematics in the annual examination. What percent of the whole class failed?
mcqs.why: Percentage failed = (Students failed / Total students) x 100 = 25/150 x 100% = 2500/150 % = 50/3 % = 16 2/3%.

mcqs.q: A car costing Rs.240,000 is reduced in price by 10%. Find the new price.
mcqs.why: Reduction = rate x original price = 10% of 240000 = (10/100) x 240000 = Rs.24,000. New price = Original Price - Reduction = 240000 - 24000 = Rs.216,000.

lessons.title: Exercises 8.1 and 8.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A constant is a fixed number whose value does not change. A variable is a letter that can take different values.
  • The coefficient is the number multiplied with the variable. The exponent (power) is the small number written above the variable; if no power is written, the exponent is 1.
  • A sentence that is correct is a true sentence and a sentence that is wrong is a false sentence.
  • Number of matches = number of matches in one box × number of boxes = 50 × number of boxes.
  • The parts of an expression joined by '+' or '−' signs are its terms. Count the parts to find the number of terms.
  • Terms having the same variables with the same exponents are like terms. Terms with different variable parts are unlike terms.

Exercise 8.1

  • Q: 1. Separate the constants and variables in the following algebraic expressions. (i) x − 5 (ii) y − 1 (iii) a + 4 (iv) x + y + 2
    Ans: Rule: A constant is a fixed number whose value does not change. A variable is a letter that can take different values.
    (i) x − 5: the letter x can take any value, so x is the variable. The number 5 is fixed, so 5 is the constant.
    (ii) y − 1: y is the variable and 1 is the constant.
    (iii) a + 4: a is the variable and 4 is the constant.
    (iv) x + y + 2: x and y are the variables and 2 is the constant.
    Answer: (i) Variable x, constant 5; (ii) Variable y, constant 1; (iii) Variable a, constant 4; (iv) Variables x and y, constant 2.
  • Q: 2. Write the co-efficients and exponents in the following expressions. (i) −2x (ii) 3y² (iii) 5z³ (iv) −6x²
    Ans: Rule: The coefficient is the number multiplied with the variable. The exponent (power) is the small number written above the variable; if no power is written, the exponent is 1.
    (i) −2x = −2 × x¹, so the coefficient is −2 and the exponent of x is 1.
    (ii) 3y² = 3 × y², so the coefficient is 3 and the exponent of y is 2.
    (iii) 5z³ = 5 × z³, so the coefficient is 5 and the exponent of z is 3.
    (iv) −6x² = −6 × x², so the coefficient is −6 and the exponent of x is 2.
    Answer: (i) Coefficient −2, exponent 1; (ii) Coefficient 3, exponent 2; (iii) Coefficient 5, exponent 3; (iv) Coefficient −6, exponent 2.
  • Q: 3. Identify true sentences, false sentences and open sentences in the following algebraic sentences. (i) 6 + 2 = 8 (ii) 3 × 5 = 16 (iii) 7x − 5 = 10 (iv) x < 3 (v) 4 ∤ 2 (vi) (11 ÷ 2) < 6
    Ans: Rule: A sentence that is correct is a true sentence and a sentence that is wrong is a false sentence. A sentence containing a variable, whose truth cannot be decided until the value of the variable is known, is an open sentence.
    (i) 6 + 2 = 8: 6 + 2 is 8, so the sentence is correct. It is a true sentence.
    (ii) 3 × 5 = 16: 3 × 5 = 15, not 16, so the sentence is wrong. It is a false sentence.
    (iii) 7x − 5 = 10: it contains the variable x and its truth depends on the value of x. It is an open sentence.
    (iv) x < 3: it contains the variable x and its truth depends on the value of x. It is an open sentence.
    (v) 4 ∤ 2: the symbol ∤ means 'does not divide'. 4 does not divide 2 exactly, so the sentence is correct. It is a true sentence.
    (vi) (11 ÷ 2) < 6: 11 ÷ 2 = 5.5 and 5.5 < 6, so the sentence is correct. It is a true sentence.
    Answer: True sentences: (i), (v), (vi); False sentence: (ii); Open sentences: (iii), (iv).
  • Q: 4. Put '=', '<' or '>' in the blank spaces to make the sentences true. (i) 5 + 3 _____ 9 (ii) 6x − 2x _____ 4x (iii) 8 − 5 _____ 2
    Ans: (i) First find the value of the left side: 5 + 3 = 8.
    Compare 8 with 9: 8 is less than 9, so the sign '<' is used.
    5 + 3 < 9
    (ii) First simplify the left side by combining like terms: 6x − 2x = 4x.
    Compare 4x with 4x: both sides are equal, so the sign '=' is used.
    6x − 2x = 4x
    (iii) First find the value of the left side: 8 − 5 = 3.
    Compare 3 with 2: 3 is greater than 2, so the sign '>' is used.
    8 − 5 > 2
    Answer: (i) < ; (ii) = ; (iii) >.
  • Q: 5. In a match box there are 50 matches. How many matches are there in (i) 2 boxes? (ii) 3 boxes? (iii) x boxes? (iv) 4x boxes? (The page shows a picture of a match box.)
    Ans: Rule: Number of matches = number of matches in one box × number of boxes = 50 × number of boxes.
    (i) In 2 boxes: 50 × 2 = 100 matches.
    (ii) In 3 boxes: 50 × 3 = 150 matches.
    (iii) In x boxes: 50 × x = 50x matches.
    (iv) In 4x boxes: 50 × 4x = 200x matches.
    Answer: (i) 100 matches (ii) 150 matches (iii) 50x matches (iv) 200x matches.

Exercise 8.2

  • Q: 1. Find the number of terms in the following algebraic expressions. (i) 6x (ii) 2 (iii) 2x + 3 (iv) 4x − 6y (v) a + b + c (vi) 2xy (vii) 7xy + 9z
    Ans: Rule: The parts of an expression joined by '+' or '−' signs are its terms. Count the parts to find the number of terms.
    (i) 6x has only one part, so it has 1 term.
    (ii) 2 has only one part, so it has 1 term.
    (iii) 2x + 3 has two parts, 2x and 3, so it has 2 terms.
    (iv) 4x − 6y has two parts, 4x and 6y, so it has 2 terms.
    (v) a + b + c has three parts, a, b and c, so it has 3 terms.
    (vi) 2xy has only one part, so it has 1 term.
    (vii) 7xy + 9z has two parts, 7xy and 9z, so it has 2 terms.
    Answer: (i) 1 (ii) 1 (iii) 2 (iv) 2 (v) 3 (vi) 1 (vii) 2.
  • Q: 2. In each of the following algebraic expressions find the like terms. (i) a² + ab + 2ab + 3a² (ii) x²y + 2xy² + 3x²y + 5xy² (iii) a³ − 2a²b + 4a²b + 5a³ (iv) xy + yz + 2xy − 3yz
    Ans: Rule: Terms having the same variables with the same exponents are like terms. Terms with different variable parts are unlike terms.
    (i) a² and 3a² have the same variable part a², so they are like terms. ab and 2ab have the same variable part ab, so they are like terms.
    (ii) x²y and 3x²y have the same variable part x²y, so they are like terms. 2xy² and 5xy² have the same variable part xy², so they are like terms.
    (iii) a³ and 5a³ have the same variable part a³, so they are like terms. −2a²b and 4a²b have the same variable part a²b, so they are like terms.
    (iv) xy and 2xy have the same variable part xy, so they are like terms. yz and −3yz have the same variable part yz, so they are like terms.
    Answer: (i) a², 3a² and ab, 2ab; (ii) x²y, 3x²y and 2xy², 5xy²; (iii) a³, 5a³ and −2a²b, 4a²b; (iv) xy, 2xy and yz, −3yz.
  • Q: 3. Write the following sum as a single term. (i) 2x + 3x (ii) 4a² + 5a² (iii) x + 2x + 3x (iv) 9ab + 2ab (v) 2xyz + 3xyz (vi) 4a³ + 7a³
    Ans: Rule: To add like terms, add their coefficients and keep the variable part unchanged.
    (i) 2x + 3x: add the coefficients 2 and 3: 2 + 3 = 5. Keep x unchanged: 5x.
    (ii) 4a² + 5a²: add the coefficients: 4 + 5 = 9. Keep a² unchanged: 9a².
    (iii) x + 2x + 3x: x means 1x. Add the coefficients: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Keep x unchanged: 6x.
    (iv) 9ab + 2ab: add the coefficients: 9 + 2 = 11. Keep ab unchanged: 11ab.
    (v) 2xyz + 3xyz: add the coefficients: 2 + 3 = 5. Keep xyz unchanged: 5xyz.
    (vi) 4a³ + 7a³: add the coefficients: 4 + 7 = 11. Keep a³ unchanged: 11a³.
    Answer: (i) 5x (ii) 9a² (iii) 6x (iv) 11ab (v) 5xyz (vi) 11a³.
  • Q: 4. Simplify the following expressions. (i) 3x + 4x + 6y (ii) x²y + 2xy² − 3x²y + 5xy² (iii) ab + bc − 2ab (iv) ax + by + cx
    Ans: Rule: Only like terms can be added or subtracted. Unlike terms are written as they are.
    (i) 3x + 4x + 6y: 3x and 4x are like terms: 3x + 4x = 7x. 6y is an unlike term and stays. Result: 7x + 6y.
    (ii) x²y + 2xy² − 3x²y + 5xy²: group the like terms: (x²y − 3x²y) + (2xy² + 5xy²). Combine: (1 − 3)x²y + (2 + 5)xy² = −2x²y + 7xy².
    (iii) ab + bc − 2ab: ab and −2ab are like terms: ab − 2ab = −ab. bc is an unlike term and stays. Result: −ab + bc.
    (iv) ax + by + cx: ax, by and cx all have different variable parts, so no terms are like terms and nothing can be combined. The expression stays the same.
    Answer: (i) 7x + 6y (ii) −2x²y + 7xy² (iii) −ab + bc (iv) ax + by + cx.
  • Q: 5. Identify the terms, like terms, coefficients and constants in the expression. (i) 3x + 4x + y − 2 (ii) 4x + 3 + 5x + y
    Ans: (i) 3x + 4x + y − 2
    Terms: the parts joined by + and − are 3x, 4x, y and −2.
    Like terms: 3x and 4x are like terms because both have variable part x.
    Coefficients: in 3x the coefficient of x is 3; in 4x the coefficient of x is 4; in y the coefficient of y is 1 (because y = 1y).
    Constant: −2 is the constant term (the term without any variable).
    (ii) 4x + 3 + 5x + y
    Terms: 4x, 3, 5x and y.
    Like terms: 4x and 5x are like terms.
    Coefficients: in 4x the coefficient of x is 4; in 5x the coefficient of x is 5; in y the coefficient of y is 1.
    Constant: 3 is the constant term.
    Answer: (i) Terms 3x, 4x, y, −2; like terms 3x and 4x; coefficients 3, 4 and 1; constant −2. (ii) Terms 4x, 3, 5x, y; like terms 4x and 5x; coefficients 4, 5 and 1; constant 3.
  • Q: 6. Match like terms. The left box shows: −4y², 17x⁴y, 6a⁴, one term whose last letters are covered by a handwritten line in the scan, 10s, −8, 6yx. The right box shows: s, 7xy, 13, 3x⁴y, 9a⁴, 7c, 6y². Match each term in the left box with the like term in the right box.
    Ans: Rule: Like terms have the same variables with the same exponents. Only the coefficients may be different. Constant terms are like terms with each other.
    −4y² has variable part y². In the right box 6y² also has variable part y², so −4y² matches 6y².
    17x⁴y has variable part x⁴y. 3x⁴y has the same variable part, so 17x⁴y matches 3x⁴y.
    6a⁴ has variable part a⁴. 9a⁴ has the same variable part, so 6a⁴ matches 9a⁴.
    10s has variable part s. The term s in the right box has the same variable part, so 10s matches s.
    −8 is a constant term. 13 is also a constant, so −8 matches 13.
    6yx has variable part yx, which is the same as xy. 7xy has variable part xy, so 6yx matches 7xy.
    The remaining left term is left with the remaining right term 7c.
    Answer: −4y² ↔ 6y²; 17x⁴y ↔ 3x⁴y; 6a⁴ ↔ 9a⁴; 10s ↔ s; −8 ↔ 13; 6yx ↔ 7xy; the partly covered term ↔ 7c.
    Note: One term in the left box is partly covered by a student's handwritten line in the available scan, so its last letters cannot be read with certainty; it is matched with the only remaining term, 7c.

mcqs.q: In the expression x - 5, what is 5 called?
mcqs.why: A constant is a fixed number whose value does not change. In x - 5, the number 5 is fixed, while x can take different values, so 5 is the constant.

mcqs.q: What are the coefficient and the exponent of x in -6x^2?
mcqs.why: Write -6x^2 = -6 x x^2. The coefficient is the number multiplied with the variable, which is -6. The exponent is the small number written above x, which is 2.

mcqs.q: The sentence 3 x 5 = 16 is which type of sentence?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Calculate the left side: 3 x 5 = 15. Step 2: Compare with 16: 15 is not equal to 16, so the sentence is wrong. A wrong sentence is a false sentence.

mcqs.q: The sentence 7x - 5 = 10 is which type of sentence?
mcqs.why: The sentence contains the variable x. Its truth cannot be decided until the value of x is known, because different values of x give different results. Such a sentence is an open sentence.

mcqs.q: Which sign makes the sentence true: 5 + 3 _____ 9?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Find the value of the left side: 5 + 3 = 8. Step 2: Compare 8 with 9. Since 8 is less than 9, the correct sign is <, so 5 + 3 < 9.

mcqs.q: One match box has 50 matches. How many matches are there in x boxes?
mcqs.why: Formula: Number of matches = matches in one box x number of boxes. Step 1: Matches in one box = 50. Step 2: Number of boxes = x. Step 3: Total = 50 x x = 50x matches.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in the expression a + b + c?
mcqs.why: Terms are the parts of an expression joined by + or - signs. Step 1: The parts are a, b and c. Step 2: Count them: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. So the expression has 3 terms.

mcqs.q: Which pair consists of like terms?
mcqs.why: Like terms have the same variables with the same exponents. Both x^2y and 3x^2y have the same variable part x^2y, so they are like terms. The other pairs have different variable parts.

mcqs.q: Write 4a^3 + 7a^3 as a single term.
mcqs.why: To add like terms, add their coefficients and keep the variable part unchanged. Step 1: Add coefficients: 4 + 7 = 11. Step 2: Keep a^3 unchanged. Result = 11a^3.

mcqs.q: Simplify x^2y + 2xy^2 - 3x^2y + 5xy^2.
mcqs.why: Step 1: Group like terms: (x^2y - 3x^2y) + (2xy^2 + 5xy^2). Step 2: Combine x^2y terms: (1 - 3)x^2y = -2x^2y. Step 3: Combine xy^2 terms: (2 + 5)xy^2 = 7xy^2. Result = -2x^2y + 7xy^2.

lessons.title: Exercises 8.3 and 8.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To add algebraic expressions, add the coefficients of like terms and keep the variable parts unchanged. Unlike terms are written as they are.
  • Write all the expressions together, group the like terms, and add their coefficients.
  • To subtract an expression, change the sign of every term of the expression being subtracted, then add the like terms.
  • If a '+' sign comes before a bracket, the signs inside do not change. If a '−' sign comes before a bracket, the sign of every term inside the bracket changes. Then combine like terms.
  • To evaluate an expression, replace each variable by its given value and then calculate.
  • Replace x by 4 everywhere and then calculate step by step.

Exercise 8.3

  • Q: 1. Add the following expressions: (i) x + y, 2x + 3y (ii) 2x + 4y, 3x + 5y, 6x + y (iii) x² + y² + z², 6x² + 2y² + 3z² (iv) x² + 2x + 3, 4x² + 6x − 5
    Ans: Rule: To add algebraic expressions, add the coefficients of like terms and keep the variable parts unchanged. Unlike terms are written as they are.
    (i) (x + y) + (2x + 3y) = x + y + 2x + 3y
    Group like terms: = (x + 2x) + (y + 3y)
    Add coefficients: = (1 + 2)x + (1 + 3)y = 3x + 4y.
    (ii) (2x + 4y) + (3x + 5y) + (6x + y) = 2x + 4y + 3x + 5y + 6x + y
    Group like terms: = (2x + 3x + 6x) + (4y + 5y + y)
    Add coefficients: = (2 + 3 + 6)x + (4 + 5 + 1)y = 11x + 10y.
    (iii) (x² + y² + z²) + (6x² + 2y² + 3z²) = x² + y² + z² + 6x² + 2y² + 3z²
    Group like terms: = (x² + 6x²) + (y² + 2y²) + (z² + 3z²)
    Add coefficients: = 7x² + 3y² + 4z².
    (iv) (x² + 2x + 3) + (4x² + 6x − 5) = x² + 2x + 3 + 4x² + 6x − 5
    Group like terms: = (x² + 4x²) + (2x + 6x) + (3 − 5)
    Add coefficients: = 5x² + 8x − 2.
    Answer: (i) 3x + 4y (ii) 11x + 10y (iii) 7x² + 3y² + 4z² (iv) 5x² + 8x − 2.
  • Q: 2. Find the sums of the following expressions. (i) 2x² + 3x + 2, 4x² − 5x + 4, 6x² + 8x − 1 (ii) 7a² − ab + b², 8a² − 3ab − 2b², 4a² + 8ab + 4b² (iii) p² + 4pq + q², 2p² − 3pq + 5q², 3p² + pq − 2q²
    Ans: Rule: Write all the expressions together, group the like terms, and add their coefficients.
    (i) (2x² + 3x + 2) + (4x² − 5x + 4) + (6x² + 8x − 1)
    = 2x² + 3x + 2 + 4x² − 5x + 4 + 6x² + 8x − 1
    Group like terms: = (2x² + 4x² + 6x²) + (3x − 5x + 8x) + (2 + 4 − 1)
    Add coefficients: = 12x² + 6x + 5.
    (ii) (7a² − ab + b²) + (8a² − 3ab − 2b²) + (4a² + 8ab + 4b²)
    = 7a² − ab + b² + 8a² − 3ab − 2b² + 4a² + 8ab + 4b²
    Group like terms: = (7a² + 8a² + 4a²) + (−ab − 3ab + 8ab) + (b² − 2b² + 4b²)
    Add coefficients: = 19a² + 4ab + 3b².
    (iii) (p² + 4pq + q²) + (2p² − 3pq + 5q²) + (3p² + pq − 2q²)
    = p² + 4pq + q² + 2p² − 3pq + 5q² + 3p² + pq − 2q²
    Group like terms: = (p² + 2p² + 3p²) + (4pq − 3pq + pq) + (q² + 5q² − 2q²)
    Add coefficients: = 6p² + 2pq + 4q².
    Answer: (i) 12x² + 6x + 5 (ii) 19a² + 4ab + 3b² (iii) 6p² + 2pq + 4q².
  • Q: 3. Subtract the first expression from the second in the following. (i) x + 3y from 4x − y (ii) x² + 3xy + y² from 3x² − 5xy − 2y² (iii) a²b + b²c + ac² from 4a²b − 2b²c + 6ac²
    Ans: Rule: To subtract an expression, change the sign of every term of the expression being subtracted, then add the like terms.
    (i) (4x − y) − (x + 3y) = 4x − y − x − 3y
    Group like terms: = (4x − x) + (−y − 3y) = 3x − 4y.
    (ii) (3x² − 5xy − 2y²) − (x² + 3xy + y²) = 3x² − 5xy − 2y² − x² − 3xy − y²
    Group like terms: = (3x² − x²) + (−5xy − 3xy) + (−2y² − y²) = 2x² − 8xy − 3y².
    (iii) (4a²b − 2b²c + 6ac²) − (a²b + b²c + ac²) = 4a²b − 2b²c + 6ac² − a²b − b²c − ac²
    Group like terms: = (4a²b − a²b) + (−2b²c − b²c) + (6ac² − ac²) = 3a²b − 3b²c + 5ac².
    Answer: (i) 3x − 4y (ii) 2x² − 8xy − 3y² (iii) 3a²b − 3b²c + 5ac².
  • Q: 4. Simplify: (i) (x + y) + (2x − y) (ii) (a²b − b²) − (2a²b + 3b²) (iii) (x²y + 2) − (2x²y + 5y² + 6) (iv) (6m² + 3n) − (2m² + 5n)
    Ans: Rule: If a '+' sign comes before a bracket, the signs inside do not change. If a '−' sign comes before a bracket, the sign of every term inside the bracket changes. Then combine like terms.
    (i) (x + y) + (2x − y) = x + y + 2x − y
    Group like terms: = (x + 2x) + (y − y) = 3x + 0 = 3x.
    (ii) (a²b − b²) − (2a²b + 3b²) = a²b − b² − 2a²b − 3b²
    Group like terms: = (a²b − 2a²b) + (−b² − 3b²) = −a²b − 4b².
    (iii) (x²y + 2) − (2x²y + 5y² + 6) = x²y + 2 − 2x²y − 5y² − 6
    Group like terms: = (x²y − 2x²y) − 5y² + (2 − 6) = −x²y − 5y² − 4.
    (iv) (6m² + 3n) − (2m² + 5n) = 6m² + 3n − 2m² − 5n
    Group like terms: = (6m² − 2m²) + (3n − 5n) = 4m² − 2n.
    Answer: (i) 3x (ii) −a²b − 4b² (iii) −x²y − 5y² − 4 (iv) 4m² − 2n.

Exercise 8.4

  • Q: 1. Find the value of the following if x = 6, y = 5 and z = 2. (i) x + y (ii) 2x (iii) 3x + y
    Ans: Rule: To evaluate an expression, replace each variable by its given value and then calculate.
    (i) x + y: replace x by 6 and y by 5: = 6 + 5 = 11.
    (ii) 2x: replace x by 6: = 2 × 6 = 12.
    (iii) 3x + y: replace x by 6 and y by 5: = 3 × 6 + 5 = 18 + 5 = 23.
    Answer: (i) 11 (ii) 12 (iii) 23.
  • Q: 2. If x = 4, evaluate the following. (i) 4x² (ii) 3x² − 4x (iii) x + 1/x
    Ans: Rule: Replace x by 4 everywhere and then calculate step by step.
    (i) 4x² = 4 × (4)² = 4 × 16 = 64.
    (ii) 3x² − 4x = 3 × (4)² − 4 × 4 = 3 × 16 − 16 = 48 − 16 = 32.
    (iii) x + 1/x = 4 + 1/4 = 16/4 + 1/4 = 17/4.
    Answer: (i) 64 (ii) 32 (iii) 17/4.
  • Q: 3. If x = 1, y = 2 find the value of the following algebraic expressions. (i) x²y + 2 (ii) x² − 2x + 3y (iii) 1/2 x + 1/3 y
    Ans: Rule: Replace x by 1 and y by 2 and then calculate.
    (i) x²y + 2 = (1)² × 2 + 2 = 1 × 2 + 2 = 2 + 2 = 4.
    (ii) x² − 2x + 3y = (1)² − 2 × 1 + 3 × 2 = 1 − 2 + 6 = 5.
    (iii) 1/2 x + 1/3 y = 1/2 × 1 + 1/3 × 2 = 1/2 + 2/3 = 3/6 + 4/6 = 7/6.
    Answer: (i) 4 (ii) 5 (iii) 7/6.
  • Q: 4. If x = 1, y = 2 and z = −1 then find the value of the following expressions: (i) 4xyz (ii) x + 2y − 3z (iii) (x + y)² − (y − z)²
    Ans: Rule: Replace x by 1, y by 2 and z by −1 and then calculate, taking care of the signs.
    (i) 4xyz = 4 × 1 × 2 × (−1) = −8.
    (ii) x + 2y − 3z = 1 + 2 × 2 − 3 × (−1) = 1 + 4 + 3 = 8.
    (iii) (x + y)² − (y − z)² = (1 + 2)² − (2 − (−1))² = (3)² − (3)² = 9 − 9 = 0.
    Answer: (i) −8 (ii) 8 (iii) 0.
  • Q: 5. Evaluate the following by taking a = 1, b = 0, c = −1. (i) ab − c (ii) [(a − c)/(a + b)] + ab (iii) a³ + b³ + c³
    Ans: Rule: Replace a by 1, b by 0 and c by −1 and then calculate.
    (i) ab − c = 1 × 0 − (−1) = 0 + 1 = 1.
    (ii) [(a − c)/(a + b)] + ab = [(1 − (−1))/(1 + 0)] + 1 × 0 = [2/1] + 0 = 2 + 0 = 2.
    (iii) a³ + b³ + c³ = (1)³ + (0)³ + (−1)³ = 1 + 0 + (−1) = 0.
    Answer: (i) 1 (ii) 2 (iii) 0.

mcqs.q: Add the expressions (x + y) and (2x + 3y).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Write together: x + y + 2x + 3y. Step 2: Group like terms: (x + 2x) + (y + 3y). Step 3: Add coefficients: (1 + 2)x + (1 + 3)y = 3x + 4y.

mcqs.q: Find the sum: (2x + 4y) + (3x + 5y) + (6x + y).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Group like terms: (2x + 3x + 6x) + (4y + 5y + y). Step 2: Add x coefficients: 2 + 3 + 6 = 11, giving 11x. Step 3: Add y coefficients: 4 + 5 + 1 = 10, giving 10y. Result = 11x + 10y.
Step 1: Group like terms: (x^2 + 6x^2) + (y^2 + 2y^2) + (z^2 + 3z^2). Step 2: Add coefficients: (1 + 6) = 7, (1 + 2) = 3, (1 + 3) = 4. Result = 7x^2 + 3y^2 + 4z^2.
Step 1: Group like terms: (x^2 + 4x^2) + (2x + 6x) + (3 - 5). Step 2: Add coefficients: (1 + 4) = 5, (2 + 6) = 8, and 3 - 5 = -2. Result = 5x^2 + 8x - 2.

mcqs.q: Find the sum of (2x^2 + 3x + 2), (4x^2 - 5x + 4) and (6x^2 + 8x - 1).
Subtract (x + 3y) from (4x - y).
mcqs.why: To subtract, change the sign of every term being subtracted, then add. Step 1: (4x - y) - (x + 3y) = 4x - y - x - 3y. Step 2: Group: (4x - x) + (-y - 3y). Step 3: Combine: 3x - 4y.

mcqs.q: Simplify (x + y) + (2x - y).
mcqs.why: A + sign before a bracket does not change the signs inside. Step 1: Open brackets: x + y + 2x - y. Step 2: Group like terms: (x + 2x) + (y - y). Step 3: Combine: 3x + 0 = 3x.

mcqs.q: If x = 6 and y = 5, what is the value of 3x + y?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Replace x by 6 and y by 5: 3 x 6 + 5. Step 2: Multiply first: 3 x 6 = 18. Step 3: Add: 18 + 5 = 23. So the value is 23.

mcqs.q: If x = 4, what is the value of 3x^2 - 4x?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Replace x by 4: 3 x (4)^2 - 4 x 4. Step 2: Find the power: (4)^2 = 16. Step 3: Multiply: 3 x 16 = 48 and 4 x 4 = 16. Step 4: Subtract: 48 - 16 = 32.

mcqs.q: If a = 1, b = 0 and c = -1, what is the value of a^3 + b^3 + c^3?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Replace each value: (1)^3 + (0)^3 + (-1)^3. Step 2: Find each power: (1)^3 = 1, (0)^3 = 0, (-1)^3 = -1. Step 3: Add: 1 + 0 + (-1) = 0.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 8
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • First open the brackets (multiply each term inside by the number outside, changing signs where a '−' comes before the bracket), then combine like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients.
  • Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate step by step.
  • A fixed number such as 5 is a constant; a letter such as x that can take different values is a variable.
  • The coefficient is the number multiplied with the variable, for example the coefficient in 3x is 3.
  • Terms are the parts joined by + or - signs; like terms have the same variables with the same exponents, while x^2 and x are unlike terms.
  • x + y is an algebraic expression, and a wrong statement such as 3 < 0 is a false sentence.
  • To simplify, open brackets first (a minus before a bracket changes every sign inside), then combine like terms.

Review Exercise 8

  • Fill in the blank: 1. Fill in the blanks. (i) The number '5' is called constant.
  • Fill in the blank: 1. Fill in the blanks. (ii) 'x' is called variable.
  • Fill in the blank: 1. Fill in the blanks. (iii) In a + b number of terms equal to 2 (two).
  • Fill in the blank: 1. Fill in the blanks. (iv) The coefficient in 3x is 3.
  • True or False: 2. Encircle 'T' if the statement is correct and encircle 'F' if it is false. (i) The number of terms in x² + 3x is two. — True
  • True or False: 2. Encircle 'T' if the statement is correct and encircle 'F' if it is false. (ii) 7 < 16 is true sentence. — True
  • True or False: 2. Encircle 'T' if the statement is correct and encircle 'F' if it is false. (iii) 6x − 4x = 2x is true sentence. — True
  • True or False: 2. Encircle 'T' if the statement is correct and encircle 'F' if it is false. (iv) x² and x are like terms. — False — x² and x are unlike terms because the exponents of x are different (2 and 1).
  • MCQ: 3. Choose the correct answer. (i) x + y is an algebraic
    (a) expression   (b) sentence   (c) equation
    Correct answer: expression
  • MCQ: 3. Choose the correct answer. (ii) 3 < 0
    (a) true sentence   (b) false sentence   (c) open sentence
    Correct answer: false sentence
  • MCQ: 3. Choose the correct answer. (iii) x²y and xy² are
    (a) like terms   (b) unlike terms   (c) constants
    Correct answer: unlike terms
  • MCQ: 3. Choose the correct answer. (iv) Number of terms in the expression 2x² + 3x + 4 is/are
    (a) one   (b) two   (c) three
    Correct answer: three
  • Q: 4. Simplify each of the following algebraic expressions by combining like terms. (i) 5x − 8x (ii) 5y − 2 − 8y − 6 (iii) 2(3a − 6) − 4(4a + 6) (iv) (6 − t) − 4(4t − 7)
    Ans: Rule: First open the brackets (multiply each term inside by the number outside, changing signs where a '−' comes before the bracket), then combine like terms by adding or subtracting their coefficients.
    (i) 5x − 8x = (5 − 8)x = −3x.
    (ii) 5y − 2 − 8y − 6: group like terms: = (5y − 8y) + (−2 − 6) = −3y − 8.
    (iii) 2(3a − 6) − 4(4a + 6): open brackets: = 6a − 12 − 16a − 24. Group like terms: = (6a − 16a) + (−12 − 24) = −10a − 36.
    (iv) (6 − t) − 4(4t − 7): open brackets: = 6 − t − 16t + 28. Group like terms: = (−t − 16t) + (6 + 28) = −17t + 34 = 34 − 17t.
    Answer: (i) −3x (ii) −3y − 8 (iii) −10a − 36 (iv) 34 − 17t.
  • Q: 5. Evaluate each of the following algebraic expressions. (i) 3x − 4y + z when x = 2, y = −3, z = −5 (ii) 8(x − 6y) when x = 5 and y = 3
    Ans: Rule: Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate step by step.
    (i) 3x − 4y + z with x = 2, y = −3, z = −5:
    = 3 × 2 − 4 × (−3) + (−5)
    = 6 + 12 − 5
    = 13.
    (ii) 8(x − 6y) with x = 5, y = 3:
    = 8 × (5 − 6 × 3)
    = 8 × (5 − 18)
    = 8 × (−13)
    = −104.
    Answer: (i) 13 (ii) −104.

mcqs.q: x + y is an algebraic:
mcqs.why: x + y is a combination of variables joined by an operation sign, with no equality or inequality sign. Such a combination is called an algebraic expression, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: 3 < 0 is a:
mcqs.why: Step 1: Compare the numbers: 3 is greater than 0, so 3 is not less than 0. Step 2: The statement 3 < 0 is therefore wrong. A wrong statement is a false sentence, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: x^2y and xy^2 are:
mcqs.why: Like terms must have the same variables with the same exponents. In x^2y the exponent of x is 2, while in xy^2 the exponent of x is 1, so the variable parts differ. They are unlike terms, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: The number of terms in the expression 2x^2 + 3x + 4 is:
mcqs.why: Terms are the parts joined by + or - signs. Step 1: The parts are 2x^2, 3x and 4. Step 2: Count them: there are 3 parts. So the number of terms is three, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: The number 5 is called a:
mcqs.why: A constant is a fixed number whose value does not change. The number 5 always has the same value, so 5 is called a constant.

mcqs.q: The letter x in an algebraic expression is called a:
mcqs.why: A variable is a letter that can take different values. The letter x can stand for many different numbers, so x is called a variable.

mcqs.q: How many terms are there in a + b?
mcqs.why: Terms are the parts joined by + or - signs. Step 1: The parts of a + b are a and b. Step 2: Count them: there are 2 parts. So the number of terms is 2.

mcqs.q: What is the coefficient in 3x?
mcqs.why: The coefficient is the number multiplied with the variable. Write 3x = 3 x x. The number multiplied with x is 3, so the coefficient in 3x is 3.

mcqs.q: Are x^2 and x like terms?
options: No, because x is a constant
mcqs.why: Like terms need the same variable with the same exponent. In x^2 the exponent of x is 2, but in x the exponent is 1 (x = x^1). Since 2 and 1 are different, x^2 and x are unlike terms, so the statement that they are like terms is false.

mcqs.q: Simplify 2(3a - 6) - 4(4a + 6).
mcqs.why: Step 1: Open the brackets: 2 x 3a = 6a, 2 x (-6) = -12, -4 x 4a = -16a, -4 x 6 = -24, giving 6a - 12 - 16a - 24. Step 2: Group like terms: (6a - 16a) + (-12 - 24). Step 3: Combine: -10a - 36.

lessons.title: Exercises 9.1 and 9.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A linear equation in one variable has only one variable and the exponent (power) of the variable is 1.
  • The value that balances an equation makes the left side equal to the right side. Find it by doing the same operation to both sides (balance method).
  • Put the given value in the equation. If the left side becomes equal to the right side, the equation is true for that value; otherwise it is false.
  • Equivalent equations have the same solution.

Exercise 9.1

  • Q: 1. Solve the following equations to show that they are linear equations in one variable: (i) 4x + 13 = 0 (ii) 5/7 x − 7/3 = 0 (iii) 3/2 x − 5 = 2x + 4
    Ans: Rule: A linear equation in one variable has only one variable and the exponent (power) of the variable is 1. To solve it, use the balance method: do the same operation to both sides until the variable is alone on one side.
    (i) 4x + 13 = 0 has one variable x with exponent 1, so it is a linear equation in one variable.
    Subtract 13 from both sides: 4x + 13 − 13 = 0 − 13
    4x = −13
    Divide both sides by 4: x = −13/4.
    Check: put x = −13/4 in 4x + 13: 4 × (−13/4) + 13 = −13 + 13 = 0. Correct.
    (ii) 5/7 x − 7/3 = 0 has one variable x with exponent 1, so it is a linear equation in one variable.
    Add 7/3 to both sides: 5/7 x = 7/3
    Multiply both sides by 7/5: x = 7/3 × 7/5 = 49/15.
    Check: put x = 49/15: 5/7 × 49/15 − 7/3 = 7/3 − 7/3 = 0. Correct.
    (iii) 3/2 x − 5 = 2x + 4 has one variable x with exponent 1, so it is a linear equation in one variable.
    Subtract 3/2 x from both sides: −5 = 2x − 3/2 x + 4, so −5 = 1/2 x + 4.
    Subtract 4 from both sides: −5 − 4 = 1/2 x, so −9 = 1/2 x.
    Multiply both sides by 2: x = −18.
    Check: put x = −18: LHS = 3/2 × (−18) − 5 = −27 − 5 = −32. RHS = 2 × (−18) + 4 = −36 + 4 = −32. LHS = RHS. Correct.
    Answer: (i) x = −13/4 (ii) x = 49/15 (iii) x = −18.
  • Q: 2. What should be the values of x which balance the following equations: (i) x = 0 (ii) x − 5 = 0 (iii) 2x + 1 = 3
    Ans: Rule: The value that balances an equation makes the left side equal to the right side. Find it by doing the same operation to both sides (balance method).
    (i) x = 0: the value of x is already alone on one side, so x = 0 balances the equation.
    (ii) x − 5 = 0: add 5 to both sides: x − 5 + 5 = 0 + 5, so x = 5.
    Check: 5 − 5 = 0. Correct.
    (iii) 2x + 1 = 3: subtract 1 from both sides: 2x = 3 − 1 = 2. Divide both sides by 2: x = 1.
    Check: 2 × 1 + 1 = 3. Correct.
    Answer: (i) x = 0 (ii) x = 5 (iii) x = 1.
  • Q: 3. Which of the following equations are true or false for the given values. (i) x + 5 = 9 when x = 3 (ii) y − 7 = 0 when y = 7
    Ans: Rule: Put the given value in the equation. If the left side becomes equal to the right side, the equation is true for that value; otherwise it is false.
    (i) x + 5 = 9 when x = 3: put x = 3: LHS = 3 + 5 = 8. RHS = 9. 8 ≠ 9, so the equation is false for x = 3.
    (ii) y − 7 = 0 when y = 7: put y = 7: LHS = 7 − 7 = 0. RHS = 0. LHS = RHS, so the equation is true for y = 7.
    Answer: (i) False (ii) True.

Exercise 9.2

  • Q: 1. Write any two equivalent equations of the following equations: (i) x + 3 = 0 (ii) 2x − 5 = 0 (iii) 3x + 1 = 2x (iv) 4x − 7 = x + 5
    Ans: Rule: Equivalent equations have the same solution. An equivalent equation is obtained by adding or subtracting the same number on both sides, or by multiplying or dividing both sides by the same non-zero number.
    (i) x + 3 = 0 (its solution is x = −3).
    Add 2 to both sides: x + 3 + 2 = 0 + 2, so x + 5 = 2.
    Multiply both sides by 2: 2(x + 3) = 2 × 0, so 2x + 6 = 0.
    Both new equations have the same solution x = −3, so they are equivalent to x + 3 = 0.
    (ii) 2x − 5 = 0 (its solution is x = 5/2).
    Add 5 to both sides: 2x = 5.
    Multiply both sides by 2: 4x − 10 = 0.
    Both have the same solution x = 5/2.
    (iii) 3x + 1 = 2x (its solution is x = −1).
    Add 1 to both sides: 3x + 2 = 2x + 1.
    Multiply both sides by 2: 6x + 2 = 4x.
    Both have the same solution x = −1.
    (iv) 4x − 7 = x + 5 (its solution is x = 4).
    Add 7 to both sides: 4x = x + 12.
    Multiply both sides by 2: 8x − 14 = 2x + 10.
    Both have the same solution x = 4.
    Answer: (i) x + 5 = 2 and 2x + 6 = 0 (ii) 2x = 5 and 4x − 10 = 0 (iii) 3x + 2 = 2x + 1 and 6x + 2 = 4x (iv) 4x = x + 12 and 8x − 14 = 2x + 10.
  • Q: 2. Solve the following equations and find the values of the variables. (i) x − 5 = 2 (ii) x + 9 = 11 (iii) x − 4 = −9 (iv) 3x + 1 = 7 (v) 2x − 7 = −8 (vi) 2x − 3 = x + 1 (vii) 2/3 x + 5 = x − 1/3 (viii) 2/3 x − 5/2 = −1/3 x + 1 (ix) 5 + 11y = 13y + 1 (x) 5/7 y + 3 = y + 2 (xi) 0.4x + 0.3 = 0.8x − 0.7 (xii) 0.7x + 1.2 = 1.8x − 2.1
    Ans: Rule (balance method): Whatever is done to one side of an equation must be done to the other side also, so that the equation stays balanced. At the end, check the answer by putting the value back in the original equation.
    (i) x − 5 = 2
    Add 5 to both sides: x − 5 + 5 = 2 + 5
    x = 7
    Check: 7 − 5 = 2. Correct.
    (ii) x + 9 = 11
    Subtract 9 from both sides: x + 9 − 9 = 11 − 9
    x = 2
    Check: 2 + 9 = 11. Correct.
    (iii) x − 4 = −9
    Add 4 to both sides: x − 4 + 4 = −9 + 4
    x = −5
    Check: −5 − 4 = −9. Correct.
    (iv) 3x + 1 = 7
    Subtract 1 from both sides: 3x = 7 − 1 = 6
    Divide both sides by 3: x = 6/3 = 2
    Check: 3 × 2 + 1 = 7. Correct.
    (v) 2x − 7 = −8
    Add 7 to both sides: 2x = −8 + 7 = −1
    Divide both sides by 2: x = −1/2
    Check: 2 × (−1/2) − 7 = −1 − 7 = −8. Correct.
    (vi) 2x − 3 = x + 1
    Subtract x from both sides: 2x − x − 3 = 1, so x − 3 = 1
    Add 3 to both sides: x = 1 + 3 = 4
    Check: LHS = 2 × 4 − 3 = 5; RHS = 4 + 1 = 5. Correct.
    (vii) 2/3 x + 5 = x − 1/3
    Subtract 2/3 x from both sides: 5 = x − 2/3 x − 1/3, so 5 = 1/3 x − 1/3
    Add 1/3 to both sides: 5 + 1/3 = 1/3 x, so 16/3 = 1/3 x
    Multiply both sides by 3: x = 16
    Check: LHS = 2/3 × 16 + 5 = 32/3 + 5 = 47/3; RHS = 16 − 1/3 = 47/3. Correct.
    (viii) 2/3 x − 5/2 = −1/3 x + 1
    Add 1/3 x to both sides: 2/3 x + 1/3 x − 5/2 = 1, so x − 5/2 = 1
    Add 5/2 to both sides: x = 1 + 5/2 = 7/2
    Check: LHS = 2/3 × 7/2 − 5/2 = 7/3 − 5/2 = −1/6; RHS = −1/3 × 7/2 + 1 = −7/6 + 1 = −1/6. Correct.
    (ix) 5 + 11y = 13y + 1
    Subtract 11y from both sides: 5 = 13y − 11y + 1, so 5 = 2y + 1
    Subtract 1 from both sides: 4 = 2y
    Divide both sides by 2: y = 2
    Check: LHS = 5 + 11 × 2 = 27; RHS = 13 × 2 + 1 = 27. Correct.
    (x) 5/7 y + 3 = y + 2
    Subtract 5/7 y from both sides: 3 = y − 5/7 y + 2, so 3 = 2/7 y + 2
    Subtract 2 from both sides: 1 = 2/7 y
    Multiply both sides by 7/2: y = 7/2
    Check: LHS = 5/7 × 7/2 + 3 = 5/2 + 3 = 11/2; RHS = 7/2 + 2 = 11/2. Correct.
    (xi) 0.4x + 0.3 = 0.8x − 0.7
    Subtract 0.4x from both sides: 0.3 = 0.8x − 0.4x − 0.7, so 0.3 = 0.4x − 0.7
    Add 0.7 to both sides: 1.0 = 0.4x
    Divide both sides by 0.4: x = 1.0/0.4 = 2.5
    Check: LHS = 0.4 × 2.5 + 0.3 = 1.0 + 0.3 = 1.3; RHS = 0.8 × 2.5 − 0.7 = 2.0 − 0.7 = 1.3. Correct.
    (xii) 0.7x + 1.2 = 1.8x − 2.1
    Subtract 0.7x from both sides: 1.2 = 1.8x − 0.7x − 2.1, so 1.2 = 1.1x − 2.1
    Add 2.1 to both sides: 3.3 = 1.1x
    Divide both sides by 1.1: x = 3.3/1.1 = 3
    Check: LHS = 0.7 × 3 + 1.2 = 2.1 + 1.2 = 3.3; RHS = 1.8 × 3 − 2.1 = 5.4 − 2.1 = 3.3. Correct.
    Answer: (i) x = 7 (ii) x = 2 (iii) x = −5 (iv) x = 2 (v) x = −1/2 (vi) x = 4 (vii) x = 16 (viii) x = 7/2 (ix) y = 2 (x) y = 7/2 (xi) x = 2.5 (xii) x = 3.
  • Q: 3. If 5 is added to a number then the number becomes 12. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    5 is added to the number, so the equation is: x + 5 = 12.
    Balance method: subtract 5 from both sides: x + 5 − 5 = 12 − 5
    x = 7.
    Check: 7 + 5 = 12. Correct.
    Answer: The number is 7.
  • Q: 4. If 9 is added to a number then the number becomes 25. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    9 is added to the number, so the equation is: x + 9 = 25.
    Balance method: subtract 9 from both sides: x + 9 − 9 = 25 − 9
    x = 16.
    Check: 16 + 9 = 25. Correct.
    Answer: The number is 16.
  • Q: 5. If 5 is subtracted from a number it becomes 13, find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    5 is subtracted from the number, so the equation is: x − 5 = 13.
    Balance method: add 5 to both sides: x − 5 + 5 = 13 + 5
    x = 18.
    Check: 18 − 5 = 13. Correct.
    Answer: The number is 18.
  • Q: 6. Find the number whose 3 times when subtracted from 9 becomes 12.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    3 times the number is 3x. When 3x is subtracted from 9, the result is 12, so the equation is: 9 − 3x = 12.
    Subtract 9 from both sides: −3x = 12 − 9 = 3.
    Divide both sides by −3: x = 3/(−3) = −1.
    Check: 9 − 3 × (−1) = 9 + 3 = 12. Correct.
    Answer: The number is −1.
  • Q: 7. If 5 is subtracted from 3 times a number the result is 16. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    3 times the number is 3x. When 5 is subtracted from it, the result is 16, so the equation is: 3x − 5 = 16.
    Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 16 + 5 = 21.
    Divide both sides by 3: x = 21/3 = 7.
    Check: 3 × 7 − 5 = 21 − 5 = 16. Correct.
    Answer: The number is 7.
  • Q: 8. The length of a rectangular farm is twice its breadth. If the perimeter of the rectangular farm is 321 meters, find the length and breadth of the farm.
    Ans: Let the breadth of the farm be x meters.
    The length is twice the breadth, so length = 2x meters.
    Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth), so the equation is: 2(2x + x) = 321.
    Simplify inside the bracket: 2 × 3x = 321, so 6x = 321.
    Divide both sides by 6: x = 321/6 = 53.5.
    So breadth = x = 53.5 meters.
    Length = 2x = 2 × 53.5 = 107 meters.
    Check: perimeter = 2 × (107 + 53.5) = 2 × 160.5 = 321 meters. Correct.
    Answer: Breadth = 53.5 meters, Length = 107 meters.
  • Q: 9. Age of a father is twice the age of his son. If father is 16 year older than his son, find the age of father and his son.
    Ans: Let the age of the son be x years.
    The father's age is twice the son's age, so father's age = 2x years.
    The father is 16 years older than the son, so the equation is: 2x = x + 16.
    Subtract x from both sides: 2x − x = 16, so x = 16.
    So the son's age = 16 years.
    Father's age = 2x = 2 × 16 = 32 years.
    Check: 32 is twice 16, and 32 − 16 = 16, so the father is 16 years older. Correct.
    Answer: Son = 16 years, Father = 32 years.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of the linear equation 4x + 13 = 0?
mcqs.why: A linear equation in one variable has one variable with exponent 1. Balance method: Step 1: Subtract 13 from both sides: 4x + 13 − 13 = 0 − 13, so 4x = −13. Step 2: Divide both sides by 4: x = −13/4. Check: 4 × (−13/4) + 13 = −13 + 13 = 0. Correct.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of the linear equation 5/7 x − 7/3 = 0?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Add 7/3 to both sides: 5/7 x = 7/3. Step 2: Multiply both sides by 7/5: x = 7/3 × 7/5. Step 3: x = 49/15. Check: 5/7 × 49/15 − 7/3 = 7/3 − 7/3 = 0. Correct.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of the linear equation 3/2 x − 5 = 2x + 4?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Subtract 3/2 x from both sides: −5 = 2x − 3/2 x + 4, so −5 = 1/2 x + 4. Step 2: Subtract 4 from both sides: −5 − 4 = 1/2 x, so −9 = 1/2 x. Step 3: Multiply both sides by 2: x = −18. Check: LHS = 3/2 × (−18) − 5 = −32; RHS = 2 × (−18) + 4 = −32. Correct.

mcqs.q: What value of x balances the equation x − 5 = 0?
mcqs.why: Balance method: the value that balances an equation makes the left side equal to the right side. Step 1: Add 5 to both sides: x − 5 + 5 = 0 + 5. Step 2: x = 5. Check: 5 − 5 = 0. Correct.

mcqs.q: Is the equation x + 5 = 9 true when x = 3?
options: False, because 3 + 5 = 8, which is not equal to 9
mcqs.why: Rule: Put the given value in the equation; if the left side equals the right side, the equation is true for that value. Step 1: Put x = 3: LHS = 3 + 5 = 8. Step 2: RHS = 9. Step 3: 8 ≠ 9, so the equation is false for x = 3.

mcqs.q: Which equation is equivalent to x + 3 = 0?
mcqs.why: Rule: Equivalent equations have the same solution; one is obtained by adding or subtracting the same number on both sides, or multiplying or dividing both sides by the same non-zero number. Step 1: x + 3 = 0 has solution x = −3. Step 2: Add 2 to both sides of x + 3 = 0: x + 5 = 2. Step 3: x + 5 = 2 also gives x = 2 − 5 = −3, the same solution, so it is equivalent.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of the equation 2/3 x + 5 = x − 1/3?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Subtract 2/3 x from both sides: 5 = x − 2/3 x − 1/3, so 5 = 1/3 x − 1/3. Step 2: Add 1/3 to both sides: 5 + 1/3 = 1/3 x, so 16/3 = 1/3 x. Step 3: Multiply both sides by 3: x = 16. Check: LHS = 2/3 × 16 + 5 = 47/3; RHS = 16 − 1/3 = 47/3. Correct.

mcqs.q: What is the solution of the equation 0.7x + 1.2 = 1.8x − 2.1?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Subtract 0.7x from both sides: 1.2 = 1.8x − 0.7x − 2.1, so 1.2 = 1.1x − 2.1. Step 2: Add 2.1 to both sides: 3.3 = 1.1x. Step 3: Divide both sides by 1.1: x = 3.3/1.1 = 3. Check: LHS = 0.7 × 3 + 1.2 = 3.3; RHS = 1.8 × 3 − 2.1 = 3.3. Correct.

mcqs.q: If 5 is subtracted from 3 times a number, the result is 16. What is the number?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the number be x; 3 times the number is 3x, so the equation is 3x − 5 = 16. Step 2: Add 5 to both sides: 3x = 16 + 5 = 21. Step 3: Divide both sides by 3: x = 21/3 = 7. Check: 3 × 7 − 5 = 21 − 5 = 16. Correct.

mcqs.q: The length of a rectangular farm is twice its breadth, and its perimeter is 321 meters. What is the length of the farm?
mcqs.why: Formula: Perimeter of a rectangle = 2 × (length + breadth). Step 1: Let the breadth be x meters, so the length is 2x meters. Step 2: 2(2x + x) = 321, so 2 × 3x = 321 and 6x = 321. Step 3: x = 321/6 = 53.5, so breadth = 53.5 meters. Step 4: Length = 2x = 2 × 53.5 = 107 meters. Check: 2 × (107 + 53.5) = 321 meters. Correct.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 9
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Use the balance method — do the same operation to both sides until the variable is alone on one side.
  • Replace the variable by the given value and then calculate.
  • Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate.
  • Use the balance method — the same operation on both sides.
  • Put the given value in the equation and compare the two sides.
  • The root of an equation is the value of the variable that makes the equation true. Find it by the balance method and check by putting the value back.

Review Exercise 9

  • Q: 1. Find the value of the variable, which balance the following Equations. (i) 3x + 5 = 8 (ii) 0.4y − 2.5 = 5.5
    Ans: Rule: Use the balance method — do the same operation to both sides until the variable is alone on one side.
    (i) 3x + 5 = 8
    Subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 8 − 5 = 3
    Divide both sides by 3: x = 1
    Check: 3 × 1 + 5 = 8. Correct.
    (ii) 0.4y − 2.5 = 5.5
    Add 2.5 to both sides: 0.4y = 5.5 + 2.5 = 8
    Divide both sides by 0.4: y = 8/0.4 = 20
    Check: 0.4 × 20 − 2.5 = 8 − 2.5 = 5.5. Correct.
    Answer: (i) x = 1 (ii) y = 20.
  • Q: 2. Evaluate the following expressions. (i) 2x − 5 when x = 2 (ii) 2x³ + 3x² + 5x − 3 when x = 1
    Ans: Rule: Replace the variable by the given value and then calculate.
    (i) 2x − 5 with x = 2: = 2 × 2 − 5 = 4 − 5 = −1.
    (ii) 2x³ + 3x² + 5x − 3 with x = 1: = 2 × (1)³ + 3 × (1)² + 5 × 1 − 3 = 2 + 3 + 5 − 3 = 7.
    Answer: (i) −1 (ii) 7.
  • Q: 3. Evaluate the following expressions for given values of the variables: (i) 3(x + y), when x = 5, y = −2 (ii) 8xy, when x = −7/2 and y = 3/2
    Ans: Rule: Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate.
    (i) 3(x + y) with x = 5, y = −2: = 3 × (5 + (−2)) = 3 × 3 = 9.
    (ii) 8xy with x = −7/2, y = 3/2: = 8 × (−7/2) × (3/2) = 8 × (−21/4) = −42.
    Answer: (i) 9 (ii) −42.
  • Q: 4. What should be the value of t which balance the following equations: (i) 0.4t + 0.5 = 0.3t (ii) 5/2 t − 3 = 1
    Ans: Rule: Use the balance method — the same operation on both sides.
    (i) 0.4t + 0.5 = 0.3t
    Subtract 0.3t from both sides: 0.4t − 0.3t + 0.5 = 0, so 0.1t + 0.5 = 0
    Subtract 0.5 from both sides: 0.1t = −0.5
    Divide both sides by 0.1: t = −0.5/0.1 = −5
    Check: LHS = 0.4 × (−5) + 0.5 = −2 + 0.5 = −1.5; RHS = 0.3 × (−5) = −1.5. Correct.
    (ii) 5/2 t − 3 = 1
    Add 3 to both sides: 5/2 t = 1 + 3 = 4
    Multiply both sides by 2/5: t = 4 × 2/5 = 8/5
    Check: 5/2 × 8/5 − 3 = 4 − 3 = 1. Correct.
    Answer: (i) t = −5 (ii) t = 8/5.
  • Q: 5. Determine whether the following equations are true or false for given values of the variables. (i) y − 3 = 7, when y = 10 (ii) 3/2 + 5/2 t = 1, when t = −1/5
    Ans: Rule: Put the given value in the equation and compare the two sides.
    (i) y − 3 = 7 with y = 10: LHS = 10 − 3 = 7. RHS = 7. LHS = RHS, so the equation is true for y = 10.
    (ii) 3/2 + 5/2 t = 1 with t = −1/5: LHS = 3/2 + 5/2 × (−1/5) = 3/2 − 1/2 = 2/2 = 1. RHS = 1. LHS = RHS, so the equation is true for t = −1/5.
    Answer: (i) True (ii) True.
  • Q: 6. Solve the following equations and find their roots. (i) 3/2 x − 5/2 = 1/2 (ii) 2(x − 3) = 4 (iii) 4(x + 2) = 3(x − 1) (iv) 0.37 − 0.5 = 0.2y
    Ans: Rule: The root of an equation is the value of the variable that makes the equation true. Find it by the balance method and check by putting the value back.
    (i) 3/2 x − 5/2 = 1/2
    Add 5/2 to both sides: 3/2 x = 1/2 + 5/2 = 6/2 = 3
    Multiply both sides by 2/3: x = 3 × 2/3 = 2
    Check: 3/2 × 2 − 5/2 = 3 − 5/2 = 1/2. Correct.
    (ii) 2(x − 3) = 4
    Divide both sides by 2: x − 3 = 2
    Add 3 to both sides: x = 5
    Check: 2 × (5 − 3) = 2 × 2 = 4. Correct.
    (iii) 4(x + 2) = 3(x − 1)
    Open the brackets: 4x + 8 = 3x − 3
    Subtract 3x from both sides: 4x − 3x + 8 = −3, so x + 8 = −3
    Subtract 8 from both sides: x = −3 − 8 = −11
    Check: LHS = 4 × (−11 + 2) = 4 × (−9) = −36; RHS = 3 × (−11 − 1) = 3 × (−12) = −36. Correct.
    (iv) 0.37 − 0.5 = 0.2y
    First calculate the left side: 0.37 − 0.5 = −0.13, so −0.13 = 0.2y
    Divide both sides by 0.2: y = −0.13/0.2 = −0.65
    Check: 0.2 × (−0.65) = −0.13 = 0.37 − 0.5. Correct.
    Note: As printed, the left side of (iv) has no variable term; the equation is solved exactly as printed. If the intended equation was 0.3y − 0.5 = 0.2y, its root would be y = 5.
    Answer: (i) x = 2 (ii) x = 5 (iii) x = −11 (iv) y = −0.65.
  • Q: 7. The sum of a number and 9 is −2. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    The sum of the number and 9 is −2, so the equation is: x + 9 = −2.
    Subtract 9 from both sides: x = −2 − 9 = −11.
    Check: −11 + 9 = −2. Correct.
    Answer: The number is −11.
  • Q: 8. The sum of −5 and a number is −15. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    The sum of −5 and the number is −15, so the equation is: x + (−5) = −15, that is x − 5 = −15.
    Add 5 to both sides: x = −15 + 5 = −10.
    Check: −10 + (−5) = −15. Correct.
    Answer: The number is −10.
  • Q: 9. The difference of a number and 3 is −6. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    The difference of the number and 3 is −6, so the equation is: x − 3 = −6.
    Add 3 to both sides: x = −6 + 3 = −3.
    Check: −3 − 3 = −6. Correct.
    Answer: The number is −3.
  • Q: 10. When 5 is subtracted from a number, the result is 16. Find the number.
    Ans: Let the number be x.
    When 5 is subtracted from the number, the result is 16, so the equation is: x − 5 = 16.
    Add 5 to both sides: x = 16 + 5 = 21.
    Check: 21 − 5 = 16. Correct.
    Answer: The number is 21.
  • Q: 11. Nadia is five years older than her brother Najam. The sum of their ages is 37. How old is Nadia?
    Ans: Let the age of Najam be x years.
    Nadia is five years older, so Nadia's age = (x + 5) years.
    The sum of their ages is 37, so the equation is: x + (x + 5) = 37.
    Simplify: 2x + 5 = 37.
    Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 37 − 5 = 32.
    Divide both sides by 2: x = 16.
    So Najam's age = 16 years.
    Nadia's age = x + 5 = 16 + 5 = 21 years.
    Check: 16 + 21 = 37, and 21 is 5 more than 16. Correct.
    Answer: Nadia is 21 years old.

mcqs.q: What value of x balances the equation 3x + 5 = 8?
mcqs.why: Balance method: do the same operation to both sides until the variable is alone. Step 1: Subtract 5 from both sides: 3x = 8 − 5 = 3. Step 2: Divide both sides by 3: x = 1. Check: 3 × 1 + 5 = 8. Correct.

mcqs.q: What value of y balances the equation 0.4y − 2.5 = 5.5?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Add 2.5 to both sides: 0.4y = 5.5 + 2.5 = 8. Step 2: Divide both sides by 0.4: y = 8/0.4 = 20. Check: 0.4 × 20 − 2.5 = 8 − 2.5 = 5.5. Correct.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the expression 2x − 5 when x = 2?
mcqs.why: Rule: Replace the variable by the given value and then calculate. Step 1: Put x = 2: 2x − 5 = 2 × 2 − 5. Step 2: = 4 − 5. Step 3: = −1.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the expression 2x³ + 3x² + 5x − 3 when x = 1?
mcqs.why: Rule: Replace the variable by the given value and then calculate. Step 1: Put x = 1: 2 × (1)³ + 3 × (1)² + 5 × 1 − 3. Step 2: = 2 + 3 + 5 − 3. Step 3: = 7.

mcqs.q: What is the value of 3(x + y) when x = 5 and y = −2?
mcqs.why: Rule: Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate. Step 1: Put x = 5 and y = −2: 3(x + y) = 3 × (5 + (−2)). Step 2: = 3 × 3. Step 3: = 9.

mcqs.q: What is the value of 8xy when x = −7/2 and y = 3/2?
mcqs.why: Rule: Replace each variable by its given value and then calculate. Step 1: Put x = −7/2 and y = 3/2: 8xy = 8 × (−7/2) × (3/2). Step 2: = 8 × (−21/4). Step 3: = −42.

mcqs.q: What value of t balances the equation 0.4t + 0.5 = 0.3t?
mcqs.why: Balance method: Step 1: Subtract 0.3t from both sides: 0.4t − 0.3t + 0.5 = 0, so 0.1t + 0.5 = 0. Step 2: Subtract 0.5 from both sides: 0.1t = −0.5. Step 3: Divide both sides by 0.1: t = −0.5/0.1 = −5. Check: LHS = 0.4 × (−5) + 0.5 = −1.5; RHS = 0.3 × (−5) = −1.5. Correct.

mcqs.q: What is the root of the equation 4(x + 2) = 3(x − 1)?
mcqs.why: The root of an equation is the value of the variable that makes it true. Step 1: Open the brackets: 4x + 8 = 3x − 3. Step 2: Subtract 3x from both sides: x + 8 = −3. Step 3: Subtract 8 from both sides: x = −3 − 8 = −11. Check: LHS = 4 × (−11 + 2) = −36; RHS = 3 × (−11 − 1) = −36. Correct.

mcqs.q: The sum of a number and 9 is −2. What is the number?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let the number be x; the sum of the number and 9 is −2, so the equation is x + 9 = −2. Step 2: Subtract 9 from both sides: x = −2 − 9 = −11. Check: −11 + 9 = −2. Correct.

mcqs.q: Nadia is five years older than her brother Najam, and the sum of their ages is 37. How old is Nadia?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Let Najam's age be x years, so Nadia's age is (x + 5) years. Step 2: The sum of their ages is 37: x + (x + 5) = 37, so 2x + 5 = 37. Step 3: Subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 32. Step 4: Divide both sides by 2: x = 16, so Najam is 16. Step 5: Nadia's age = x + 5 = 16 + 5 = 21 years. Check: 16 + 21 = 37. Correct.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • To add line segments, lay them end to end on one straight line with compasses; the whole length is the sum.
  • Lay the three segments end to end on one straight line with compasses; the whole length is the sum.
  • The remaining part = length of the whole segment − length cut off.
  • mCB = mAB − mAC.
  • To add line segments, lay them end to end on one straight line with compasses; the whole length is the sum of the parts.
  • The remaining part after cutting off = length of the whole segment minus the length cut off.
  • A right bisector divides a segment into two equal parts and makes an angle of 90° with it.
  • For a right bisector, use a radius more than half the segment from both ends and join the two crossing points of the arcs.
  • A perpendicular at a point on a segment uses equal arcs CP = CQ on either side of the point; a perpendicular from an outside point uses an arc from that point cutting the segment at two points.

Exercise 10.1

  • Q: Q1. Draw two line segments 3.8cm and 2.6cm long. Draw a line segment whose length is equal to the sum of the lengths of these two line segments.
    Ans: Rule: To add line segments, lay them end to end on one straight line with compasses; the whole length is the sum.
    Step 1: With a ruler draw the two given segments, AB = 3.8cm and CD = 2.6cm.
    Step 2: Draw a line XY and take a point L on it.
    Step 3: With L as centre and radius equal to AB (3.8cm), draw an arc cutting line XY at M, so LM = 3.8cm.
    Step 4: With M as centre and radius equal to CD (2.6cm), draw an arc cutting line XY at N, so MN = 2.6cm.
    Step 5: LN is the required segment.
    Calculation: LN = 3.8cm + 2.6cm = 6.4cm.
    Finished figure: On straight line XY the points L, M, N lie in order; LM is marked 3.8cm, MN is marked 2.6cm, and the whole segment LN measures 6.4cm.
    Answer: LN = 6.4cm.
  • Q: Q2. Draw three line segments 2.8cm, 3.4cm and 4.1cm long. Draw a line segment whose length is equal to the sum of the lengths of these three line segments.
    Ans: Rule: Lay the three segments end to end on one straight line with compasses; the whole length is the sum.
    Step 1: With a ruler draw the three given segments of 2.8cm, 3.4cm and 4.1cm.
    Step 2: Draw a line XY and take a point K on it.
    Step 3: With K as centre and radius 2.8cm, draw an arc cutting XY at L, so KL = 2.8cm.
    Step 4: With L as centre and radius 3.4cm, draw an arc cutting XY at M, so LM = 3.4cm.
    Step 5: With M as centre and radius 4.1cm, draw an arc cutting XY at N, so MN = 4.1cm.
    Step 6: KN is the required segment.
    Calculation: KN = 2.8cm + 3.4cm + 4.1cm = 10.3cm.
    Finished figure: On straight line XY the points K, L, M, N lie in order with KL = 2.8cm, LM = 3.4cm, MN = 4.1cm, and the whole segment KN measures 10.3cm.
    Answer: KN = 10.3cm.
  • Q: Q3. Draw AB and CD where mAB = 4.5cm and mCD = 3.5cm. Draw KL such that mKL = mAB + mCD.
    Ans: Step 1: With a ruler draw AB = 4.5cm and CD = 3.5cm.
    Step 2: Draw a line and take a point K on it.
    Step 3: With K as centre and radius equal to AB (4.5cm), draw an arc cutting the line at a point, say P, so KP = 4.5cm.
    Step 4: With P as centre and radius equal to CD (3.5cm), draw an arc cutting the line at L, so PL = 3.5cm.
    Step 5: KL is the required segment.
    Calculation: mKL = mAB + mCD = 4.5cm + 3.5cm = 8.0cm.
    Finished figure: K, P, L lie in order on one straight line; KP is marked 4.5cm, PL is marked 3.5cm, and KL measures 8.0cm.
    Answer: mKL = 8.0cm.
  • Q: Q4. Draw KL, PQ and MN such that mKL = 2.9cm, mPQ = 3.2cm and mMN = 4.1cm. Draw AB where mAB = mKL + mPQ + mMN.
    Ans: Step 1: With a ruler draw KL = 2.9cm, PQ = 3.2cm and MN = 4.1cm.
    Step 2: Draw a line XY and take a point A on it.
    Step 3: With A as centre and radius equal to KL (2.9cm), draw an arc cutting XY at a point, say P, so AP = 2.9cm.
    Step 4: With P as centre and radius equal to PQ (3.2cm), draw an arc cutting XY at a point, say Q, so PQ' (from P to Q) = 3.2cm.
    Step 5: With Q as centre and radius equal to MN (4.1cm), draw an arc cutting XY at B, so QB = 4.1cm.
    Step 6: AB is the required segment.
    Calculation: mAB = 2.9cm + 3.2cm + 4.1cm = 10.2cm.
    Finished figure: A, P, Q, B lie in order on one straight line with the three parts 2.9cm, 3.2cm and 4.1cm, and the whole segment AB measures 10.2cm.
    Answer: mAB = 10.2cm.
  • Q: Q5. Draw a line segment 5.2cm long. Cut off a segment 2.3cm long from it. Find the measure of the remaining part of the given segment.
    Ans: Rule: The remaining part = length of the whole segment − length cut off.
    Step 1: With a ruler draw segment AB = 5.2cm.
    Step 2: With A as centre and radius 2.3cm, draw an arc cutting AB at C, so AC = 2.3cm is the part cut off.
    Step 3: CB is the remaining part.
    Calculation: mCB = mAB − mAC
    = 5.2cm − 2.3cm
    = 2.9cm.
    Finished figure: Segment AB of 5.2cm with point C on it 2.3cm from A; the part CB from C to B is left.
    Answer: The remaining part measures 2.9cm.
  • Q: Q6. Draw AB such that mAB = 6.5cm. Cut off AC such that mAC = 2cm. What is the length of CB?
    Ans: Rule: mCB = mAB − mAC.
    Step 1: With a ruler draw AB = 6.5cm.
    Step 2: With A as centre and radius 2cm, draw an arc cutting AB at C, so AC = 2cm.
    Step 3: CB is the remaining part.
    Calculation: mCB = 6.5cm − 2cm = 4.5cm.
    Finished figure: Segment AB of 6.5cm with point C on it 2cm from A; CB runs from C to B.
    Answer: mCB = 4.5cm.
  • Q: Q7. Draw line segments of the following lengths: (i) 4.8cm (ii) 5.4cm (iii) 6.6cm. Draw their right bisectors by using compasses and ruler.
    Ans: A right bisector divides a segment into two equal parts and makes an angle of 90° with it. The same steps are used for each segment.
    For each segment, say AB:
    Step 1: With a ruler draw AB of the given length — (i) 4.8cm, (ii) 5.4cm, (iii) 6.6cm.
    Step 2: With A as centre and radius more than half of AB, draw arcs above and below AB.
    Step 3: With B as centre and the same radius, draw arcs cutting the first arcs at P (above) and Q (below).
    Step 4: Join P to Q with a ruler. Line PQ cuts AB at its midpoint R.
    Step 5: PQ is the right bisector of AB; ∠PR A = 90° and AR = RB.
    Check of the halves: (i) 4.8 ÷ 2 = 2.4cm each half; (ii) 5.4 ÷ 2 = 2.7cm each half; (iii) 6.6 ÷ 2 = 3.3cm each half.
    Finished figure (for each part): A horizontal segment AB crossed at its midpoint R by a vertical line PQ, with equal crossing arcs shown above at P and below at Q.
  • Q: Q8. Draw line segments of the following lengths: (i) 3.5cm (ii) 4.4cm (iii) 5.5cm. Take a point on each segment and draw perpendiculars to the given line segments. (Use ruler and compasses only)
    Ans: The same steps are used for each segment.
    For each segment, say AB, with point C on it:
    Step 1: With a ruler draw AB of the given length — (i) 3.5cm, (ii) 4.4cm, (iii) 5.5cm — and mark a point C on AB.
    Step 2: With C as centre and any suitable radius, draw arcs cutting AB at P on one side of C and Q on the other side, so CP = CQ.
    Step 3: With P as centre and radius more than half of PQ, draw an arc above AB.
    Step 4: With Q as centre and the same radius, draw an arc cutting the first arc at R.
    Step 5: Join C to R with a ruler and produce it.
    Step 6: CR is the required perpendicular, so CR ⊥ AB at C and ∠RCA = ∠RCB = 90°.
    Finished figure (for each part): Segment AB with point C on it, equal marks at P and Q on either side of C, and a vertical line through C meeting the crossing arcs at R above the segment.
  • Q: Q9. Draw line segments of the following lengths: (i) 4.5cm (ii) 5.2cm (iii) 3.8cm. Take a point outside each segment and draw perpendicular to the given segments from that point. (Use ruler and compasses only).
    Ans: The same steps are used for each segment.
    For each segment, say AB, with point C outside it:
    Step 1: With a ruler draw AB of the given length — (i) 4.5cm, (ii) 5.2cm, (iii) 3.8cm — and take a point C outside (above) AB.
    Step 2: With C as centre and a suitable radius (large enough to reach AB), draw an arc cutting AB at P and Q.
    Step 3: With P as centre and a suitable radius, draw an arc on the opposite side of AB from C.
    Step 4: With Q as centre and the same radius, draw an arc cutting the arc of Step 3 at S.
    Step 5: Join C to S with a ruler; line CS cuts AB at R.
    Step 6: CR is the required perpendicular, so CR ⊥ AB and ∠CRP = 90°.
    Finished figure (for each part): Segment AB with point C above it, a long arc from C crossing AB at P and Q, two crossing arcs below AB meeting at S, and the line from C through R on AB down to S, at right angles to AB.

mcqs.q: Two segments measure 3.8 cm and 2.6 cm. They are laid end to end on one straight line to form segment LN. What is the length of LN?
mcqs.why: To add line segments, lay them end to end on one straight line. LN = LM + MN. Step 1: LM = 3.8 cm. Step 2: MN = 2.6 cm. Step 3: LN = 3.8 cm + 2.6 cm = 6.4 cm.

mcqs.q: Three segments measure 2.8 cm, 3.4 cm and 4.1 cm. Laid end to end they form segment KN. What is the length of KN?
mcqs.why: The whole length is the sum of the three parts laid end to end. Step 1: 2.8 cm + 3.4 cm = 6.2 cm. Step 2: 6.2 cm + 4.1 cm = 10.3 cm. So KN = 2.8 cm + 3.4 cm + 4.1 cm = 10.3 cm.

mcqs.q: If mAB = 4.5 cm and mCD = 3.5 cm, and KL is drawn so that mKL = mAB + mCD, what is mKL?
mcqs.why: mKL = mAB + mCD. Step 1: Substitute the values: mKL = 4.5 cm + 3.5 cm. Step 2: Add: 4.5 + 3.5 = 8.0. So mKL = 8.0 cm, with KP = 4.5 cm and PL = 3.5 cm on one straight line.

mcqs.q: Segments KL, PQ and MN measure 2.9 cm, 3.2 cm and 4.1 cm. Segment AB is drawn with mAB = mKL + mPQ + mMN. What is mAB?
mcqs.why: mAB = mKL + mPQ + mMN. Step 1: 2.9 cm + 3.2 cm = 6.1 cm. Step 2: 6.1 cm + 4.1 cm = 10.2 cm. So mAB = 2.9 cm + 3.2 cm + 4.1 cm = 10.2 cm.

mcqs.q: A segment AB is 5.2 cm long. A part AC of 2.3 cm is cut off from it. What is the measure of the remaining part CB?
mcqs.why: The remaining part = length of the whole segment minus the length cut off. mCB = mAB - mAC. Step 1: mAB = 5.2 cm and mAC = 2.3 cm. Step 2: mCB = 5.2 cm - 2.3 cm = 2.9 cm.

mcqs.q: AB is 6.5 cm long and AC = 2 cm is cut off from it. What is the length of CB?
mcqs.why: Rule: mCB = mAB - mAC. Step 1: Substitute: mCB = 6.5 cm - 2 cm. Step 2: Subtract: 6.5 - 2 = 4.5. So the remaining part CB measures 4.5 cm.

mcqs.q: A segment of 4.8 cm is divided by its right bisector. What is the length of each half?
mcqs.why: A right bisector divides a segment into two equal parts and makes an angle of 90 degrees with it. Step 1: Length of segment = 4.8 cm. Step 2: Each half = 4.8 cm divided by 2 = 2.4 cm. So AR = RB = 2.4 cm.

mcqs.q: What angle does a right bisector make with the segment it bisects?
mcqs.why: By definition a right bisector cuts a segment at its midpoint at right angles. In the construction, line PQ cuts AB at midpoint R with angle PRA = 90 degrees and AR = RB, so the angle is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: To draw the right bisector of AB, what radius is used from centres A and B to draw the arcs above and below AB?
mcqs.why: Step fact from the construction: with A as centre and radius more than half of AB, draw arcs above and below AB, then with B as centre and the same radius draw arcs cutting them at P and Q. Joining P to Q gives the right bisector.

mcqs.q: A perpendicular is drawn at point C on segment AB using ruler and compasses. With C as centre, arcs cut AB at P and Q. What is true about CP and CQ?
mcqs.why: Step fact from the construction: with C as centre and any suitable radius, arcs are drawn cutting AB at P on one side of C and Q on the other side, so the distances are equal: CP = CQ. The line CR then satisfies CR perpendicular to AB at C.

lessons.title: Exercises 10.2 and 10.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Copying an angle with compasses transfers the same arc and the same chord distance PQ, so the copy equals the original.
  • Doubling steps the same chord distance twice along one arc; bisecting gives angle ÷ 2, and dividing into four gives angle ÷ 4 by bisecting twice.
  • Compass-only angles are built from 60° steps: 90° = 60° + 30°, 150° = 120° + 30°, 165° = 180° − 15°, 135° = 90° + 45°, 105° = 90° + 15°.
  • Triangle constructions: SSS (three sides), SAS (two sides and included angle), ASA (two angles and included side), RHS (right angle, hypotenuse and one side).
  • Before an SSS construction, check the triangle rule: the sum of any two sides must be greater than the third side; the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.

Exercise 10.2

  • Q: Q1. Construct angles of the following measures with the help of protractor: (i) 65° (ii) 73° (iii) 55°. Construct angles equal in measure to these angles by using compasses and ruler.
    Ans: Part 1 — with a protractor (same method for each angle):
    Step 1: Draw a ray BC and place the centre of the protractor at B with its base line along BC.
    Step 2: Read the required measure on the protractor scale — (i) 65°, (ii) 73°, (iii) 55° — and mark a point A at that mark.
    Step 3: Remove the protractor and join B to A. ∠ABC is the required angle.
    Part 2 — copying the angle with compasses and ruler only (same method for each angle, for a given ∠ABC copied as ∠XYZ):
    Step 1: With centre B and a suitable radius, draw an arc cutting BC at P and BA at Q.
    Step 2: Draw a ray YZ. With centre Y and the same radius, draw an arc cutting YZ at R.
    Step 3: Measure the distance PQ with the compasses. With R as centre and radius equal to PQ, draw an arc cutting the arc of Step 2 at S.
    Step 4: Join Y to S and produce to X. ∠XYZ is the required angle.
    Finished figure: Beside each protractor-drawn angle stands an identical copied angle with the same opening, made only with compass arcs.
    Answer: The copied angles measure (i) 65°, (ii) 73°, (iii) 55°, equal to the given angles.
  • Q: Q2. Construct angles of the following measures with the help of protractor: (i) 35° (ii) 42° (iii) 70°. Construct angles twice in measure of the given angles by using compasses and ruler.
    Ans: Part 1 — with a protractor: Draw a ray, place the protractor centre at its end point, mark (i) 35°, (ii) 42°, (iii) 70° respectively, and join to get each given angle, say ∠PQR.
    Part 2 — doubling with compasses and ruler (same method for each angle; double of ∠PQR made at B on ray BC as ∠ABC):
    Step 1: With centre Q and a suitable radius, draw an arc cutting QR at X and QP at Y.
    Step 2: Draw ray BC. With centre B and the same radius, draw an arc cutting BC at K.
    Step 3: Set the compasses to the distance XY. With K as centre and radius XY, draw an arc cutting the arc of Step 2 at L.
    Step 4: Without changing the radius XY, with L as centre draw a second consecutive arc cutting the same arc at M.
    Step 5: Join B to M and produce to A. ∠ABC is the required angle, twice ∠PQR.
