    Ans: Method: In a pie graph the bigger the angle of a sector, the greater the number it represents. The sectors are: Goats 180°, Cows 120°, Chickens 60° (180 + 120 + 60 = 360°).
    (i) The biggest angle is 180°, for Goats.
    Answer: (i) Goats are greatest in number.
    (ii) The smallest angle is 60°, for Chickens.
    Answer: (ii) Chickens are smallest in number.
    (iii) Method: Ratio of goats and cows = angle of goats : angle of cows = 180 : 120. Divide both by 60: 180 ÷ 60 = 3 and 120 ÷ 60 = 2, so the ratio is 3 : 2.
    Answer: (iii) The ratio of goats and cows is 3 : 2.
  • Q: 2. Aslam obtained marks in different subjects as given in the pie graph. Read the graph and answer the following questions. The sectors of the pie graph are: Maths 110°, Science 90°, English 75°, Urdu 45°, Islamiyat 40°. (i) In which subject did he obtain maximum marks? (ii) In which subject did he obtain minimum marks? (iii) Without calculation, find ratio between the marks he obtained in Science and Urdu.
    Ans: Method: In a pie graph the bigger the angle of a sector, the more marks it represents. The sectors are: Maths 110°, Science 90°, English 75°, Urdu 45°, Islamiyat 40° (110 + 90 + 75 + 45 + 40 = 360°).
    (i) The biggest angle is 110°, for Maths.
    Answer: (i) He obtained maximum marks in Maths.
    (ii) The smallest angle is 40°, for Islamiyat.
    Answer: (ii) He obtained minimum marks in Islamiyat.
    (iii) Method: Ratio of Science and Urdu marks = angle of Science : angle of Urdu = 90 : 45. Divide both by 45: 90 ÷ 45 = 2 and 45 ÷ 45 = 1, so the ratio is 2 : 1.
    Answer: (iii) The ratio between the marks in Science and Urdu is 2 : 1.

mcqs.q: What is grouped data?
options: Raw data arranged in different groups
A list of single separate values
Data shown only in a pie graph
mcqs.why: Grouped data is raw data when it is put in some order or arranged in different groups. For example, 50 students divided into score groups 0-20, 20-40 and so on form grouped data.

mcqs.q: The marks 95, 94, 93, 92 and 91 obtained by 5 students are an example of:
mcqs.why: Ungrouped data is numerical facts obtained as such, in their original form and not arranged in groups. These marks are given just as obtained, one by one, so they are ungrouped data.

mcqs.q: The ages of kidney patients are listed as 40, 36, 17, 25, 12, 13, 31 and so on, one by one. What type of data is this?
mcqs.why: Data given as a plain list of separate values, not arranged in groups or classes, is ungrouped data. The ages are listed one by one as obtained and are not put into any groups, so this is ungrouped data.

mcqs.q: Marks of 40 students are shown in groups 15-20, 21-26, 27-32, 33-38, 39-44 and 45-50 with the number of students in each group. Qasim Shah calls it grouped data and Yasmin calls it ungrouped data. Who is correct?
mcqs.why: When raw data is arranged in different groups (classes) with the number of observations in each group, it is grouped data. The marks here are arranged in the groups 15-20 up to 45-50, so Qasim Shah is correct.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph data for the speed of a car, what was the speed in the 4th hour?
mcqs.why: The data given for the car is: 1st hour 50 km, 2nd hour 100 km, 3rd hour 150 km and 4th hour 200 km. So the speed in the 4th hour was 200 km, shown by the tallest bar.

mcqs.q: For the rainfall bar graph of Peshawar, the scale used along the vertical axis is 1 big square = ?
mcqs.why: For the rainfall graph the scale chosen along OY is 1 big square = 5 mm of rainfall, marking 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30, so that all values from April 15 mm to September 30 mm can be shown.

mcqs.q: Wheat production in Charsadda was: 1990: 90 tons, 1991: 100 tons, 1992: 115 tons, 1993: 120 tons, 1994: 110 tons. In which year was production the highest?
mcqs.why: Step 1: List the values: 90, 100, 115, 120, 110. Step 2: Find the greatest value: 120 is greater than all the others. Step 3: 120 tons was produced in 1993, so production was highest in 1993.

mcqs.q: In the pie chart 'A student's typical day' (Sleep 7 h, Work 8 h, TV 2 h, Hobbies 3.5 h, Meals 2 h, Other 1.5 h), which activity took the most time?
mcqs.why: Step 1: Compare all the times: 7, 8, 2, 3.5, 2 and 1.5 hours. Step 2: The greatest value is 8 hours. Step 3: 8 hours belongs to Work, so Work took the most time and has the biggest sector.

mcqs.q: In the travel-to-work survey (Drive 40%, Bus 25%, Train 20%, Walk 10%, Cycle 5%), what fraction of the people travel by bus?
mcqs.why: Formula: Fraction = percentage / 100, then simplify. Step 1: Bus = 25%. Step 2: Write as a fraction: 25/100. Step 3: Divide top and bottom by 25: 25/100 = 1/4. So 1/4 of the people travel by bus.

mcqs.q: Ahmad's pie graph shows Goats 180 degrees, Cows 120 degrees and Chickens 60 degrees. What is the ratio of goats to cows?
mcqs.why: Formula: Ratio in a pie graph = angle of goats : angle of cows. Step 1: Write the angles: 180 : 120. Step 2: Divide both by 60: 180 / 60 = 3 and 120 / 60 = 2. So the ratio of goats to cows is 3 : 2.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 13
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Data is the set of numerical facts obtained from observation and experiments, and data is of two types: grouped and ungrouped.
  • A graph shows the relationship between two different quantities.
  • In a bar graph the width of all bars is equal, with equal spaces between the bars.
  • A pie graph, also called a circular graph, is divided into sectors; the whole circle equals 100 percent.
  • The sum of the measures of the angles in a pie graph is 360 degrees, and the bigger sector angle represents the greater value.

Review Exercise 13

  • Fill in the blank: 1(i). Fill in the blanks. Graph shows relationship between two different quantities.
  • Fill in the blank: 1(ii). Fill in the blanks. Data is set of numerical facts.
  • Fill in the blank: 1(iii). Fill in the blanks. There are two types of data.
  • Fill in the blank: 1(iv). Fill in the blanks. The whole circle for pie graphs equals 100 percent.
  • Fill in the blank: 1(v). Fill in the blanks. Sum of measures of angles in pie graph = 360°.
  • MCQ: 2(i). Choose the correct answer. Numerical facts obtained from observation and experiments are called.
    (a) Figure   (b) Data   (c) Frequency   (d) Classes
    Correct answer: Data
  • MCQ: 2(ii). Choose the correct answer. Data is of
    (a) One type   (b) Two types   (c) Three types   (d) Four types
    Correct answer: Two types
  • MCQ: 2(iii). Choose the correct answer. In bar graph width of bars is
    (a) Equal   (b) Greater than first bar   (c) Less than first bar   (d) Unequal
    Correct answer: Equal
  • MCQ: 2(iv). Choose the correct answer. Pie graph is also known as
    (a) Bar graph   (b) Circular graph   (c) Rectangular graph   (d) Line graph
    Correct answer: Circular graph
  • MCQ: 2(v). Choose the correct answer. Sum of measures of angles in pie-graph is
    (a) 90°   (b) 180°   (c) 270°   (d) 360°
    Correct answer: 360°
  • MCQ: 2(vi). Choose the correct answer. Pie graph is divided into
    (a) Sectors   (b) Rectangles   (c) Chords   (d) Squares
    Correct answer: Sectors
  • Q: 3. Following are the ages (years) of 30 students of a school. 16, 13, 12, 14, 8, 9, 15, 4, 7, 6, 11, 10, 7, 5, 6, 14, 13, 10, 9, 8, 7, 5, 4, 16, 13, 12, 9, 6, 5, 7. Identify the type of data.
    Ans: Method: Data given as a plain list of separate values, not arranged in groups or classes, is ungrouped data.
    The 30 ages are listed one by one as obtained and are not put into any groups.
    Answer: This is ungrouped data.
  • Q: 4. Draw a vertical bar graph to represent number of admission in a school in different classes in different years. Detail is given below. Years: 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005. No. of admission: 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100.
    Ans: Data: 2000: 50; 2001: 60; 2002: 70; 2003: 80; 2004: 90; 2005: 100.
    Method: For a vertical bar graph, draw two mutually perpendicular rays OX (horizontal) and OY (vertical) meeting at O.
    Step 1: Show the years (2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005) along OX at equal gaps.
    Step 2: Choose the scale along OY: 1 big square = 10 admissions, marking 0, 10, 20, ... up to 100.
    Step 3: Draw bars of equal width with equal spaces between them, with heights: 2000 = 50, 2001 = 60, 2002 = 70, 2003 = 80, 2004 = 90, 2005 = 100.
    The six bars, reaching 50, 60, 70, 80, 90 and 100 on the admissions axis, form the required vertical bar graph.
  • Q: 5. The means of different students to go to school are shown in pie graph, read the graph and answer the following questions. The sectors of the pie graph are: Bicycle 120°, On foot 90°, Bus 90°, Van 60°. (i) In how many sectors pie graph has been divided? (ii) Which means is mostly used for going to school? (iii) Which means is less used for going to school?
    Ans: Method: In a pie graph the bigger the angle of a sector, the more it is used. The sectors are: Bicycle 120°, On foot 90°, Bus 90°, Van 60° (120 + 90 + 90 + 60 = 360°).
    (i) Count the sectors in the pie graph: Bicycle, On foot, Bus and Van = 4 sectors.
    Answer: (i) The pie graph has been divided into 4 sectors.
    (ii) The biggest angle is 120°, for Bicycle.
    Answer: (ii) Bicycle is mostly used for going to school.
    (iii) The smallest angle is 60°, for Van.
    Answer: (iii) Van is less used for going to school.

mcqs.q: Numerical facts obtained from observation and experiments are called:
mcqs.why: Numerical facts obtained from observation and experiments are called data, as keyed in the book. Figures, frequency and classes are other terms used while handling data, not the facts themselves.

mcqs.q: Data is of how many types?
mcqs.why: Data is of two types: grouped data and ungrouped data, as keyed in the book. Grouped data is arranged in groups, while ungrouped data is given as obtained.

mcqs.q: In a bar graph, the width of the bars is:
mcqs.why: In a bar graph all bars are drawn with the same width and with equal spaces between them, as keyed in the book. Only the heights or lengths of the bars change with the values.

mcqs.q: A pie graph is also known as a:
mcqs.why: A pie graph is drawn in the shape of a circle divided into sectors, so it is also known as a circular graph, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: The sum of the measures of the angles in a pie graph is:
mcqs.why: A pie graph is a full circle. The angles around the centre of a circle add up to 360 degrees, so the sum of the measures of the angles in a pie graph is 360 degrees, as keyed in the book.

mcqs.q: A pie graph is divided into:
mcqs.why: A pie graph is a circle divided into parts called sectors, and each sector represents one part of the data, as keyed in the book. The bigger the sector angle, the greater the value it shows.

mcqs.q: A graph shows the relationship between two different:
mcqs.why: A graph shows the relationship between two different quantities, for example time and speed, or months and rainfall. One quantity is shown along one axis and the other quantity along the other axis.

mcqs.q: The whole circle in a pie graph equals how many percent?
mcqs.why: In a pie graph the whole circle represents the complete data, which is 100 percent. Each sector is a part of that 100 percent, and the sector angles together make the full 360 degrees.

mcqs.q: The ages of 30 students are listed as 16, 13, 12, 14, 8, 9, 15 and so on, one by one. What type of data is this?
mcqs.why: Data given as a plain list of separate values, not arranged in groups or classes, is ungrouped data. The 30 ages are listed one by one as obtained and are not put into any groups, so this is ungrouped data.

mcqs.q: In a pie graph of means of going to school (Bicycle 120 degrees, On foot 90 degrees, Bus 90 degrees, Van 60 degrees), which means is mostly used?
mcqs.why: In a pie graph the bigger the angle of a sector, the more it is used. Step 1: Compare the angles: 120, 90, 90 and 60 degrees. Step 2: The biggest angle is 120 degrees, which is for Bicycle. So Bicycle is mostly used.
